definition_zh: 不诚实地；以欺诈方式
definition_en: in a way that is not truthful, or by cheating
core_image: 一只手把账本上的数字轻轻改小一格
scene: 他把账本上的数字往小改了一格，又把笔放回原处。 He dishonestly claimed that the money was lost.
sceneCN: 这里 dishonestly 指「不诚实地」（第 1 个义项：以不老实的方式）；句意是他不诚实地声称那笔钱丢了。

collocations.zh: 以不正当手段取得钱财

senses.title: In an untruthful way
senses.definition: in a way that is not truthful
senses.definitionCN: 以不说真话的方式
senses.example: He answered dishonestly.
senses.exampleCN: 他回答得不老实。
senses.why: A small turn of the pen can move a large sum.
senses.whyCN: 笔尖轻轻一转，能挪动一大笔钱。

senses.title: By cheating or fraud
senses.definition: by cheating or by breaking the rules of fair dealing
senses.definitionCN: 靠欺骗或破坏公平规则
senses.example: The money was obtained dishonestly.
senses.exampleCN: 那笔钱是不正当取得的。
senses.why: What the law calls fraud, the mouth calls a mistake.
senses.whyCN: 法律叫欺诈的事，嘴上叫失误。

intro.en: Dishonestly is dishonest plus -ly, and dishonest is dis- added to Latin honestus, honourable.
intro.cn: dishonestly 是 dishonest 加 -ly；dishonest 则是把 dis- 加在拉丁语 honestus（可敬的）上。

items.en: Honestus meant honourable, from honos, honour.
items.cn: honestus 意为可敬的，其根是 honos（荣誉）。

items.en: Honest first meant honourable in English.
items.cn: honest 在英语里最初意为可敬的。

items.en: The adverb honest-ly named the manner of acting.
items.cn: 副词 honest-ly 用来指行事的方式。

items.en: Dis- turned the manner into its opposite.
items.cn: 前缀 dis- 把这种方式翻成反面。

items.en: Dishonestly now covers lies in speech and in accounts.
items.cn: 今天 dishonestly 既指言语上的谎，也指账目上的假。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the honest stem, and the meaning group names other manners of cheating.
note.cn: 形近组共享 honest 词干，近义组列出别的欺骗方式。

entries.definition: not truthful or fair
the quality of being truthful
a lie or a cheating act
in a way that uses lies
by illegal trickery
in a way that is not just

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with one stroke of a pen and end with a short sum in the book.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从笔下的一划开始，落到账上少掉的一笔。

normal.en: Dishonest plus -ly turns the fault into a manner.
normal.cn: dishonest 加 -ly，把毛病变成一种方式。

normal.en: A form filled dishonestly is a lie with boxes.
normal.cn: 不实填写的表格，是带方格的谎。

normal.en: Money gained dishonestly leaves a long shadow.
normal.cn: 不正当得来的钱，留下很长的影子。

normal.en: He dealt dishonestly once and lost ten clients.
normal.cn: 他欺诈过一次，失去了十个客户。

normal.en: A witness who answers dishonestly answers twice.
normal.cn: 证人若不实回答，就得再答一次。

abstract.en: Picture a figure made smaller by one stroke.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数字被一笔改小。

abstract.en: Picture a pen set down too carefully.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔被过分小心地放下。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt folded into a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据被折进口袋。

examples.en: He dishonestly claimed that the money was lost.
examples.cn: 他不诚实地声称那笔钱丢了。

examples.en: The clerk dealt dishonestly with every customer.
examples.cn: 那名职员对每位顾客都不老实。

examples.en: Goods were obtained dishonestly and returned.
examples.cn: 货物是以不正当手段取得的，已被退回。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dishonestly 记成「不体面地」：dis 是否定，honest 是可敬、老实，-ly 表方式，用不老实的方式做事就是不诚实地。

root: 由 dishonesty 与 -ly 构成，源头是拉丁语 honestus（可敬的）与 honos（荣誉）。字面意思是「以失去可敬的方式」，英语里用来指说话不实或用骗术取利的具体做法。

sensesIntro.en: From the manner of a lying answer to the manner of a false account.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一句不实回答的方式，到一本假账的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure in a ledger quietly made smaller by one stroke.
core.cn: 核心意象：账本上一个数字被一笔悄悄改小。

branches.en: The first sense is the manner of an untrue answer.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是不实回答的那种方式。

branches.en: The second sense is the manner of a cheat or a fraud.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是行骗或欺诈的方式。

branches.en: Both senses describe how an act is done, not what it is.
branches.cn: 两个义项说的都是做法，而不是事情本身。

branches.en: Both need a listener who trusts the speaker.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要一个相信说话人的听者。

branches.en: Only the second sense can be tried in a court.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项能在法庭上受审。

intro.en: Dishonestly is the adverb built on honest, inside the Latin honos family.
intro.cn: dishonestly 是由 honest 构成的副词，属于拉丁语 honos 一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin honos, honour, gives honestus, then honest; dis- and -ly turn it into a manner of acting.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 honos（荣誉）给出 honestus，再成为 honest；dis- 与 -ly 把它变成一种行事方式。

items.exampleCN: 这项声明是不实作出的。
一笔不诚实的交易黄了。
不诚实之风蔓延整个办公室。

definition_zh: 托儿所；育婴室；苗圃；培养地
definition_en: a place where young children are cared for, a place where young plants are raised and sold, and by extension any place that shelters early growth
core_image: 玻璃棚下一排排嫩苗舒展开叶片，等着一双粗糙的手把它们移进大田
scene: 三月清晨的温室里，一位老花农把刚冒芽的小苗一株株移进木箱。 Before the last frost, he moved every seedling into a warm nursery.
sceneCN: 这里的 nursery 是「苗圃」（第 2 个义项：培育并出售幼苗的地方）；句意为在最后一场霜来临前，他把每株幼苗都搬进了温暖的苗圃。图中可辨识物件：玻璃棚、木箱、嫩苗。

pos.zh: 托儿所；育婴室；苗圃；培养地

derivatives.zh: 由动词 nurse 加 -ing 构成，义为「护理；看护」
由 nurse 与 maid 复合而成，义为「保姆；照看孩子的女佣」
由 nursery 与 man 复合而成，义为「苗圃经营者；花木培育者」

senses.title: A place where young children are cared for
senses.definition: a room or small building where babies and very young children are looked after while their parents are at work
senses.definitionCN: 父母上班时照看婴儿和幼儿的房间或小建筑
senses.example: The baby spends the morning at a nursery near the office.
senses.exampleCN: 宝宝上午在办公室附近的一家托儿所度过。
senses.why: The word grew from nurse, the person who feeds and tends a child, and the -ery ending names a place, so a nursery is first of all where nursing happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从 nurse（喂养并照看孩子的人）长出来，-ery 后缀标出一个场所，所以 nursery 首先是「照护发生的地方」。

senses.title: A place where young plants are raised
senses.definition: a place, often with glasshouses, where young plants are grown and sold to gardeners
senses.definitionCN: 通常带有温室的场所，在那里培育幼苗并出售给园艺爱好者
senses.example: She bought a small apple tree from a local nursery.
senses.exampleCN: 她从当地一家苗圃买了一棵小苹果树。
senses.why: Nursing is not only for children: the same care applied to weak young plants produced this sense, because a nursery is wherever early life is kept alive.
senses.whyCN: 照护不只针对孩子：把同样的呵护用在娇弱的幼苗上，就生出这个义项，因为苗圃正是让早期生命存活下来的地方。

senses.title: A place or environment that develops talent
senses.definition: a place or environment where a particular kind of person, skill or idea is developed early and protected
senses.definitionCN: 某类人、技能或想法早期得到发展并受到保护的地方或环境
senses.example: The small club became a nursery for young musicians.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小俱乐部成了年轻音乐人的培养地。
senses.why: Once a nursery is a sheltered place for beginnings, any institution that raises talent early can borrow the word, so schools and clubs use it too.
senses.whyCN: 既然 nursery 指为「开端」提供庇护的场所，任何早早培养人才的机构都能借这个词，于是学校与俱乐部也用它。

senses.title: A child's room in an old-fashioned house
senses.definition: a room in a house, especially an old-fashioned one, where the children sleep and play
senses.definitionCN: 宅子里供孩子睡觉和玩耍的房间，尤指老式住宅中的儿童房
senses.example: The old house still had a nursery with a rocking chair.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老宅里还留着一间放着摇椅的儿童室。
senses.why: Before public care existed, looking after small children was a room inside the home, so the place meaning of -ery turned inward and named a domestic room.
senses.whyCN: 在公共托育出现之前，照看幼儿只是宅子里的一间房，于是 -ery 的「场所」义指向室内，命名了一间家庭用房。

intro.en: Nursery is an English formation from nurse plus the place suffix -ery; nurse itself goes back through Old French to Latin words for nourishing.
intro.cn: nursery 是英语用 nurse 加场所后缀 -ery 造出的词；nurse 本身经古法语上溯到拉丁语中表示「滋养」的词。

items.en: Nutrire meant to feed, suckle and nourish, and it described the bodily care given to the very young.
items.cn: nutrire 意为喂养、哺乳、滋养，描述的是给予幼小者的身体照料。

items.en: A nutrix was a wet nurse, the woman who fed and tended another woman's baby, so the word carried both feeding and caring.
items.cn: nutrix 指乳母，即喂养并照看别人家婴儿的女子，这个词同时带着「喂」与「护」两层意思。

items.en: Old French norrice kept the sense of a woman who suckles and cares for a child, and English borrowed it as nurse.
items.cn: 古法语 norrice 保留了「哺乳并照看孩子的女子」这一意思，英语借入后写作 nurse。

items.en: English added -ery, a suffix for a place or a collective activity, so nursery named the place where nursing was done.
items.cn: 英语加上表示场所或一类活动的后缀 -ery，于是 nursery 命名了「照护发生的场所」。

items.en: Modern English spread nursery from the child's room to the childcare centre and then to the garden, where young plants receive the same tending.
items.cn: 现代英语让 nursery 从孩子的房间扩展到托育机构，再扩展到花园，在那里幼苗得到同样的照料。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on nurse; the near-meaning group collects places that care for the very young or for young plants.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 nurse 之上的词；近义组收照看幼儿或培育幼苗的场所。

entries.definition: A person trained to care for the sick, or one who feeds and tends a child.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练照护病人的人，或喂养照看孩子的人。

entries.definition: The work or profession of caring for sick people.
entries.definitionCN: 照护病人的工作或职业；护理。

entries.definition: A woman employed to look after young children.
entries.definitionCN: 受雇照看幼儿的女佣；保姆。

entries.definition: A person who grows and sells young plants.
entries.definitionCN: 培育并出售幼苗的人；苗圃经营者。

entries.definition: A school or class for children from about three to six years old.
entries.definitionCN: 约三到六岁儿童就读的学校或班级；幼儿园。

entries.definition: A place where babies are cared for during the day.
entries.definitionCN: 白天照看婴儿的场所；托儿所。

entries.definition: A glass building used for growing plants that need warmth.
entries.definitionCN: 用于栽培需要温暖植物的玻璃建筑；温室。

entries.definition: An area of soil where seeds are sown and young plants begin to grow.
entries.definitionCN: 播下种子、幼苗开始生长的一块土壤。

normalIntro.en: Nursery is nurse turned into a place, and the -ery suffix keeps the idea of a spot set aside for care.
normalIntro.cn: nursery 是把 nurse 变成场所的说法，-ery 后缀保留了「专门划出来照护的一处地方」这个意思。

normal.en: Nurse means to feed and tend, and -ery means a place, so nursery is literally a tending place.
normal.cn: nurse 意为喂养和照看，-ery 意为场所，所以 nursery 字面上就是「照看的地方」。

normal.en: Nursery school and day nursery keep the child-care sense: one for older toddlers, one for babies.
normal.cn: nursery school 与 day nursery 都保留育儿义：一个收较大的幼儿，一个收婴儿。

normal.en: Plant nursery moved the same care outdoors, because seedlings need shelter as much as infants do.
normal.cn: plant nursery 把同一种照料搬到户外，因为幼苗和婴儿一样需要庇护。

normal.en: Nursery rhyme survives from the old sense of a child's room, where such songs were sung.
normal.cn: nursery rhyme 保留了「孩子的房间」这个旧义，那些歌谣正是在那里唱的。

normal.en: Nurseryman adds man to nursery, naming the person who tends plants in such a place.
normal.cn: nurseryman 在 nursery 后加 man，指出在这个场所里照看植物的人。

abstract.en: A nursery is a protected interval in the life of something small, before it must face the open field.
abstract.cn: 苗圃是一样小东西生命中被保护起来的一段时间，之后它才必须面对开阔的田野。

abstract.en: One word for babies and seedlings suggests that early growth, human or green, asks for the same conditions.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时指婴儿和幼苗，说明无论是人还是植物，早期生长都需要相似的条件。

abstract.en: Calling a club a nursery admits that talent, like a seedling, needs a sheltered first season.
abstract.cn: 把一个俱乐部称作 nursery，就是承认才能也像幼苗一样，需要有一个受庇护的第一季。

examples.en: The twins were dropped off at the nursery before eight.
examples.cn: 双胞胎八点前被送到托儿所。

examples.en: This nursery sells young fruit trees in spring.
examples.cn: 这家苗圃春天出售幼小的果树。

examples.en: That little theatre was a nursery for several famous actors.
examples.cn: 那座小剧场是几位著名演员的成长摇篮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呐，莎莉」——妈妈把孩子交给托儿所老师时喊着名字；记住 nursery 是托儿所。

root: nurse（照护者）加表示场所的后缀 -ery 构成；nurse 经古法语 norrice 上溯拉丁语 nutrire（滋养）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a sheltered place for early life; the senses divide between children, plants, talent and the old room inside a house.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是为早期生命提供庇护的场所；义项分指孩子、植物、才能，以及宅子里那间旧式的儿童室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of seedlings under glass, waiting for a rough hand to move them into the open field.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃棚下一排排嫩苗，等着一双粗糙的手把它们移进大田。

branches.en: a cot in a bright room while parents are at work
branches.cn: 父母上班时，明亮房间里的一张婴儿床

branches.en: glasshouses full of green shoots for sale
branches.cn: 满是待售绿苗的温室

branches.en: a small stage where beginners learn their craft
branches.cn: 初学者磨练技艺的小舞台

branches.en: an old house with a rocking chair by the window
branches.cn: 老宅里窗边放着摇椅的房间

branches.en: the same sheltering care given to babies and to seedlings
branches.cn: 给予婴儿与幼苗的同一种庇护式照护

intro.en: The word joins a Latin verb of feeding, an Old French nurse, and an English suffix that turns an activity into a place.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示喂养的拉丁动词、古法语的「乳母」，以及把活动变成场所的英语后缀接在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin nutrire and nutrix are recorded and give the whole family its sense of feeding and care.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nutrire 与 nutrix 有记录，为这一族词提供了「喂养与照护」的意思。

items.meaning: a woman who suckles a child
one who cares for the young or sick; to tend
a place where an activity is carried out
a place of nursing or plant raising
a maid who looks after children
a person connected with a place or trade
items.meaningCN: 与某场所或行业有关的人

definition_zh: 超过；超出；胜过
definition_en: to be greater than a limit or to do better than others
core_image: 赛跑选手冲线时越过计分板上的旧纪录
scene: 马拉松终点前，一名选手越过了赛会保持多年的纪录。 Her time exceeded the old record by two seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 exceed 是「超过」（第 1 个义项：在数量或程度上大于）；句意：马拉松终点前，一名选手越过了赛会保持多年的纪录。

senses.title: Being greater
senses.definition: to be more than a number or limit
senses.definitionCN: 在数量上大于某个数字或限度
senses.example: The cost exceeded our budget.
senses.exampleCN: 费用超出了我们的预算。
senses.why: The verb marks a step past a fixed line.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词标记跨过一条固定的线。

senses.title: Going beyond
senses.definition: to go past what is allowed
senses.definitionCN: 越过被允许的界限
senses.example: He was fined for exceeding the speed limit.
senses.exampleCN: 他因超速被罚款。
senses.why: Crossing a limit is the same step, now against rules.
senses.whyCN: 越界是同一个动作，只是这次触犯了规则。

senses.title: Doing better
senses.definition: to do better than someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 表现得比某人或某物更好
senses.example: She exceeded all her rivals in the final round.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一轮中胜过了所有对手。
senses.why: Outrunning others is exceeding them.
senses.whyCN: 跑在别人前面就是胜过他们。

intro.en: Exceed comes from Latin excedere, to go out or go beyond.
intro.cn: exceed 源自拉丁语 excedere，意为走出、越过。

items.en: Cedere means to go or yield.
items.cn: cedere 意为走或让出。

items.en: Excedere joins ex-, out, with cedere, to go.
items.cn: excedere 由 ex-（出）与 cedere（走）组成。

items.en: Old French exceder keeps the sense of going beyond.
items.cn: 古法语 exceder 保留了越过的含义。

items.en: English exceed means to pass a limit.
items.cn: 英语 exceed 意为越过限度。

items.en: It now covers numbers, limits and rivals.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖数字、限度与对手。

note.en: Exceed is the verb; excess is the noun for too much.
note.cn: exceed 是动词，excess 是表示「过量」的名词。

entries.definition: an amount that is too much
much more than is needed
to an extreme degree
to be better or greater than
to do better than someone
to pass someone in front

normalIntro.en: To exceed is to step out past a line.
normalIntro.cn: exceed 就是跨出界线一步。

normal.en: Excess is the noun from exceed.
normal.cn: excess 是 exceed 对应的名词。

normal.en: Excessive means far too much.
normal.cn: excessive 意为过多。

normal.en: To exceed the limit is to cross it.
normal.cn: exceed the limit 就是越过界限。

normal.en: Sales exceeded expectations last year.
normal.cn: 去年销售额超出预期。

normal.en: Exceed and excess share the same root.
normal.cn: exceed 与 excess 同根。

abstract.en: Picture a runner's foot landing past the line.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者的脚落在终点线之外。

abstract.en: Imagine a glass filled beyond its rim.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子被倒得溢过杯口。

abstract.en: Think of an arrow flying past the target.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭飞过靶子。

examples.en: The bill exceeded what we had planned.
examples.cn: 账单超出了我们的计划。

examples.en: Demand for the tickets far exceeded supply.
examples.cn: 门票需求远远超过供给。

examples.en: He exceeded the speed limit on the highway.
examples.cn: 他在高速公路上超速了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ ceed（走）」——走出界限，就是超过。

root: 拉丁语 excedere（走出）＝ ex-（出）＋ cedere（走）→ 古法语 exceder → exceed，核心义「走出既定的界线」。

sensesIntro.en: Exceed means to be greater than a number, to pass an allowed limit, or to do better than others.
sensesIntro.cn: exceed 意为在数量上更大、越过允许的界限或胜过他人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot landing beyond the finish line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚落在终点线之外。

branches.en: Stepping past the line makes a number too large.
branches.cn: 跨过界线使数字变得过大。

branches.en: The same step breaks an allowed limit.
branches.cn: 同一个动作越过了允许的限度。

branches.en: Outrunning a rival is also exceeding.
branches.cn: 跑在对手前面也是 exceed。

branches.en: Numbers and rules both draw lines to pass.
branches.cn: 数字与规则都划出可被越过的线。

branches.en: Being greater and doing better share one image.
branches.cn: 数量更大与表现更好共用同一个意象。

intro.en: Exceed combines ex-, out, with Latin cedere, to go.
intro.cn: exceed 由 ex-（出）与拉丁语 cedere（走）组成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb excedere, to go out, passes through French into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 excedere（走出）经法语进入英语。

items.exampleCN: cedere 出现在 proceed 中。

items.example: Cede is the short English form.
items.exampleCN: cede 是简短的英语形式。

items.example: Exceed keeps the sense of stepping out.
items.exampleCN: exceed 保留了走出的含义。

items.example: Excess names the result of passing.
items.exampleCN: excess 指越过后产生的结果。

items.example: Proceed shares the same cedere root.
items.exampleCN: proceed 共享同一个 cedere 词根。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cedere 是 proceed 与 exceed 的基础。

latinEntries.example: Excedere is the source of exceed.
latinEntries.exampleCN: excedere 是 exceed 的来源。

definition_zh: 巢；窝；（鸟、昆虫等的）巢穴；一窝（雏鸟、卵）；筑巢；嵌套；窝藏
definition_en: a structure built or hollowed out by an animal for laying eggs and raising young
core_image: 树杈间一只用泥与草茎抹成的碗，内壁被压得光滑，四枚带斑点的卵并排躺在正中
scene: 孩子在谷仓梁上发现了一个旧巢，里面还留着去年的一片蛋壳。 A sparrow's nest sat wedged against the beam, three eggs warm inside it.
sceneCN: 这里 nest 指「鸟巢、窝」（第 1 个义项：动物为产卵育雏而筑的结构）；句意为一只麻雀的巢卡在梁边，里面三枚卵还是温的；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 筑巢；巢居；嵌套；层层套放

senses.title: A structure built to hold eggs
senses.titleCN: 为盛放卵而筑成的结构
senses.definition: a structure of twigs, mud, grass or other material in which a bird lays and incubates eggs
senses.definitionCN: 用树枝、泥、草等材料筑成、鸟在其中产卵与孵卵的结构
senses.example: A sparrow's nest sat wedged against the beam.
senses.exampleCN: 一只麻雀的巢卡在梁边。
senses.why: the core sense is simply the object, because everything else the word names is derived from this built container.
senses.whyCN: 核心义就是这件物体，因为这个词命名的其它一切都是由这个容器引申出来的。

senses.title: The home of a whole brood
senses.definition: the place where a brood is reared, viewed as the young family's home
senses.definitionCN: 一窝雏被养育之处，被看作这个幼小家庭的家
senses.example: The whole nest begged whenever the adult landed.
senses.exampleCN: 成鸟一落下，整窝雏鸟都乞食。
senses.why: the container and its occupants merge, so nest may name the family inside as much as the structure.
senses.whyCN: 容器与其居住者合并，因此 nest 既可指结构，也可指里面的全家。

senses.title: A clutch counted as one unit
senses.definition: the set of eggs laid in one nest and incubated together
senses.definitionCN: 在同一巢中产出并一起孵化的一组卵
senses.example: Rangers recorded a nest of four eggs under the lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 巡护员在灯下记录到一窝四枚卵。
senses.why: counting by nests is convenient because the nest defines the set, so the container becomes the unit of number.
senses.whyCN: 以巢计数很方便，因为巢定义了这一组，容器于是成了计数单位。

senses.title: A hollow made by another animal
senses.titleCN: 由其它动物挖出的巢穴
senses.definition: a burrow, hole or cavity used by an insect, mammal or fish for young
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫、哺乳动物或鱼为育幼而使用的洞、穴或腔
senses.example: Wasps build a paper nest under the roof tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 黄蜂在屋瓦下筑成纸质的巢。
senses.why: once the word is applied beyond birds, the structure stops being woven and becomes any prepared cavity.
senses.whyCN: 一旦越出鸟类，这个结构就不再是编织的，而成为任何备好的腔室。

senses.title: To build and occupy a nest
senses.definition: to build a nest and use it for breeding
senses.definitionCN: 建造巢并将其用于繁殖
senses.example: Swallows nest every year in the same corner of the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 燕子每年都在谷仓同一个角落筑巢。
senses.why: the verb is simply the noun turned into an action, so it means to do what the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词转为动作，意为做出名词所指的那件事。

senses.title: To place one thing inside another
senses.titleCN: 把一物套进另一物内部
senses.definition: to fit objects or structures one inside another, as boxes or data tables
senses.definitionCN: 把物件或结构放进彼此内部，如盒子或数据表
senses.example: Nest the smaller boxes inside the larger crate.
senses.exampleCN: 把小盒子套进大板条箱里。
senses.why: the technical sense generalizes the shape of the bird's cup: something held within something else.
senses.whyCN: 技术义把鸟巢的形状一般化：一物被另一物容纳在其中。

senses.title: A graduated set that fits inside itself
senses.titleCN: 可以逐层套放的一组器物
senses.definition: a set of similar objects of decreasing size that store one inside another, as a nest of tables
senses.definitionCN: 一组大小递减、可以互相套放的同类物件，如套几
senses.example: The nest of tables slotted under the largest one.
senses.exampleCN: 套几收进最大的那张下面。
senses.why: the noun is applied to objects that imitate the containment of a nest, so the name follows the shape rather than the bird.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词被用于模仿「巢的容纳关系」的物件，因此名称追随形状而非鸟。

senses.title: A den of troublesome people or things
senses.titleCN: 滋生麻烦的人或事物之处
senses.definition: a place or group seen as a breeding ground for something harmful, as in a nest of thieves
senses.definitionCN: 被视为有害之物滋生地的场所或群体，如贼窝
senses.example: The yard had become a nest of infection after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水之后这个院子成了感染滋生地。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the idea of a sheltered place where something grows, and that something is no longer young.
senses.whyCN: 比喻只保留「有遮蔽之处、某种东西在其中生长」的意思，而生长之物已不再是幼鸟。

intro.en: Nest is an Old English word, nest, with the same form in several old Germanic languages; its relation to Latin nidus is debated rather than settled.
intro.cn: nest 是古英语词 nest，在数种古老日耳曼语中形式相同；它与拉丁 nidus 的关系属争议，未有定论。

items.en: Old English nest named both the structure and the brood in it, and the word has kept that double reach.
items.cn: 古英语 nest 既指结构，也指其中的一窝，这双重范围一直保留。

items.en: Old Norse nest, Old High German nest and Middle Dutch nest show a common Germanic stock, so Latin borrowing is unlikely.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 nest、古高地德语 nest、中古荷兰语 nest 表明共同的日耳曼来源，因此不太可能是拉丁借词。

items.en: Latin nidus 'nest' looks similar and means the same, but most handbooks treat the resemblance as parallel; a shared Indo-European source is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 拉丁 nidus「巢」形似义同，但多数辞书把这种相似视为平行；共有印欧来源属重构形式。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the pre-Germanic shape of nest is unresolved; the root commonly printed for it is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：nest 在日耳曼语之前的形式无定论；常印出的词根是重构形式，并非有证材料。

items.en: The verb nest appeared later, formed directly from the noun, and was extended to any placing of one thing inside another.
items.cn: 动词 nest 出现较晚，直接由名词构成，并被扩展到任何把一物放进另一物的动作。

items.en: Phrases such as empty nest and nest egg carried the word into family life and household finance.
items.cn: empty nest、nest egg 等短语把这个词带进家庭生活与家庭理财。

note.en: Group one separates the near-synonyms for animal homes; group two separates the words built on nest itself.
note.cn: 第一组区分表示动物居所近义词；第二组区分由 nest 本身构成的词。

entries.definition: The -ing form names the building and sitting; the bare nest names the object.
entries.definitionCN: -ing 形式指建与伏的行为；原形 nest 指物件。

entries.definition: A nestling is a chick too young to leave; it is the content of the nest, not the nest.
entries.definitionCN: nestling 是尚不能离巢的雏鸟，是巢中之物，而非巢。

entries.definition: A nester is the bird regarded as the one that nests, marked by -er.
entries.definitionCN: nester 是把鸟看作筑巢者，由 -er 标记。

entries.definition: Nested describes something already placed inside another; it is a state, not a place.
entries.definitionCN: nested 描述已被放进另一物之中的状态，是状态而非地点。

entries.definition: A burrow is dug into earth or sand; a nest may be built on a branch or in a hole.
entries.definitionCN: burrow 掘入土或沙；巢可能筑在枝上或洞里。

entries.definition: A den is a mammal's shelter, often a cave or hollow, and usually not built from gathered material.
entries.definitionCN: den 是哺乳动物的居所，常为洞穴，通常不由采集材料筑成。

entries.definition: A lair is where a wild animal rests, especially a predator; it carries no idea of eggs.
entries.definitionCN: lair 是野兽尤其捕食者歇息之处，不含产卵之意。

entries.definition: A hive is the home of a bee colony, a special case of an insect nest with a fixed architecture.
entries.definitionCN: hive 是蜂群的家，是昆虫巢的一种特例，结构固定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Germanic relatives, real compounds and real idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的日耳曼同族词、真实复合词与真实习语。

normal.en: The Germanic relatives are Old Norse nest and Old High German nest, not Latin words.
normal.cn: 日耳曼同族词是古诺斯语 nest 与古高地德语 nest，而非拉丁词。

normal.en: The family runs nest, nesting, nester, nestling, nested, nest box.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nest、nesting、nester、nestling、nested、nest box。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: build a nest, leave the nest, nest of eggs.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：筑巢、离巢、一窝蛋。

normal.en: The idioms empty nest and nest egg show the word applied to family and savings.
normal.cn: 习语 empty nest 与 nest egg 显示这个词被用于家庭与储蓄。

normal.en: In computing, nest means to place one structure inside another.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，nest 指把一种结构放进另一种。

abstract.en: Picture a cup so exactly shaped that the sitter's body closes its opening.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗形制精准，伏者的身体正好封住开口。

abstract.en: Picture a house whose walls keep growing back after each departure.
abstract.cn: 想象一座屋子，每次有人离开后墙壁又重新长回。

abstract.en: Picture a set of bowls where the smallest is invisible until lifted out.
abstract.cn: 想象一套碗，最小的一只不被提起就看不见。

examples.en: The nest was rebuilt on the same branch after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，巢又在同一根枝上重建。

examples.en: She found an old nest in the rafters, empty and crumbling.
examples.cn: 她在椽子上发现一只空了的旧巢，正在崩解。

examples.en: Programmers nest these records inside a parent object.
examples.cn: 程序员把这些记录嵌进一个父对象里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nest（巢）」——树枝围成碗，卵卧其中 → 巢、窝；动作义为筑巢、套住

root: 古英语 nest「巢；一窝」，与古诺斯语、古高地德语、中古荷兰语 nest 同出日耳曼共有词；与拉丁 nidus「巢」形似义同，通常视为平行构词，共有印欧来源仅为重构形式，日耳曼以前词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: a built cup holds something precious, and the word then names the occupants, the count, a prepared cavity, a den of trouble, the act of building, any placing of one thing inside another, and finally a set of objects made to slot together.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个形状展开：一只编成的碗托住贵重之物，词语随后指其居住者、计数单位、备好的腔室、滋生麻烦的窝、建造动作、任何把一物放进另一物的动作，最后指一组可以互相套放的器物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup woven at the branch fork, its inner walls smoothed by the body inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：枝杈分叉处编成的碗，内壁被其中的身体压得光滑。

branches.en: CUP AND FAMILY: the container and the family in it are named by the same word.
branches.cn: 碗与家庭：容器与其中的家庭由同一个词命名。

branches.en: COUNTED SET: the nest defines the clutch, so the container becomes the unit.
branches.cn: 可数的组：巢定义了这一窝，容器于是成了单位。

branches.en: A SHELTERED PLACE: any animal's cavity, and a den where trouble breeds.
branches.cn: 有遮蔽之处：任何动物的腔室，以及滋生麻烦的窝。

branches.en: DOING THE NOUN: the verb is the noun turned into an act.
branches.cn: 做名词所指的事：动词就是名词转为动作。

branches.en: SHAPE EXPORTED: a rule for holding one thing inside another, and objects made to nest.
branches.cn: 形状外输：一条「一物容另一物」的规则，以及照此造出的套叠器物。

intro.en: Nest is a bare Germanic root that takes English suffixes and compounds; it has no Latin prefix structure.
intro.cn: nest 是裸露的日耳曼词根，只接英语后缀与复合成分，没有拉丁前缀结构。

latinIntro.en: Nest itself has no Latin element; the Latin entries are the learned equivalents English borrowed separately for the same content.
latinIntro.cn: nest 本身不含拉丁成分；下列拉丁条目是英语为同一内容另行借入的学术词。

items.example: They used the bonus as a nest egg.
items.exampleCN: 他们把奖金当作储备金。

items.meaning: a home after the children leave
items.example: The empty nest felt too quiet.

items.exampleCN: 志愿者挂上了四十只巢箱。

items.example: The ruling stirred a hornet's nest.

definition_zh: 熟练的；有技能的
definition_en: having the training and ability to do something well
core_image: 老师傅双手稳当地组装精密零件
scene: 这家工厂到处都需要熟练的工人。 The factory needs skilled workers everywhere.
sceneCN: 这里 skilled 是「熟练的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家工厂到处都需要熟练的工人。

senses.title: Trained and able
senses.definition: having the training and ability to do something well
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练并有能力做好某事
senses.example: The factory needs skilled workers everywhere.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂到处都需要熟练的工人。
senses.why: This describes people with learned ability.
senses.whyCN: 这描述拥有学来本领的人。

senses.title: Needing training
senses.definition: needing special training or ability
senses.definitionCN: 需要专门训练或能力的
senses.example: Welding is a skilled job.
senses.exampleCN: 焊接是一项需要专门技能的工作。
senses.why: Jobs, not only people, can be described as skilled.
senses.whyCN: 不仅人，工作也可以被形容为需要技能。

senses.title: Good at something
senses.definition: very good at doing a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 非常擅长做某件特定的事
senses.example: She is skilled at repairing old clocks.
senses.exampleCN: 她擅长修理旧钟表。
senses.why: The pattern skilled at names a specialty.
senses.whyCN: skilled at 这一搭配用来指出专长。

intro.en: Skilled is skill turned into an adjective with -ed.
intro.cn: skilled 是 skill 加 -ed 构成的形容词。

items.en: Skil meant understanding or judgment.
items.cn: skil 意为理解或判断。

items.en: Skill entered English as a noun.
items.cn: skill 作为名词进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ed formed skilled.
items.cn: 后缀 -ed 构成 skilled。

items.en: The word described trained workers.
items.cn: 这个词用来描述受过训练的工人。

items.en: It spread to jobs and specialties.
items.cn: 它的用法扩展到工作和专长。

note.en: Skilled is compared with look-alike words and words for trained ability.
note.cn: 把 skilled 与形近词以及表示训练有素能力的词作比较。

abstract.en: Skill is invisible until skilled hands move.
abstract.cn: 技能在熟练的手动起来之前是看不见的。

abstract.en: Training turns ordinary effort into skilled ease.
abstract.cn: 训练把普通的努力变成熟练的从容。

abstract.en: A skilled worker is a library of small lessons.
abstract.cn: 熟练工人是一座小小经验教训的图书馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: skilled = skill（技能）+ -ed（具有……的）；unskilled 是不熟练的，semiskilled 是半熟练的。

root: 由 skill（技能）加形容词后缀 -ed 构成；核心义「具备学来的本领」。

sensesIntro.en: Skilled describes trained people, jobs needing training, or a specific specialty.
sensesIntro.cn: skilled 形容受过训练的人、需要训练的工作，或某一专长。

core.en: Ability that has been trained into the hands.
core.cn: 经过训练进入双手的能力。

branches.en: A worker repeats a motion until it is sure.
branches.cn: 工人反复练习一个动作，直到它稳当。

branches.en: Some tasks demand long training.
branches.cn: 有些任务需要长期训练。

branches.en: A specialty grows from steady practice.
branches.cn: 专长从稳定练习中成长。

branches.en: Trained people and training-heavy jobs belong together.
branches.cn: 受过训练的人与需要训练的工作彼此相配。

branches.en: Ease reveals the hours behind it.
branches.cn: 从容透露出它背后的许多小时。

intro.en: Skilled forms words about trained and untrained ability.
intro.cn: skilled 构成表示熟练与不熟练能力的词。

latinIntro.en: The base skill is Germanic, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 skill 属日耳曼语，并非拉丁语。

definition_zh: 运行的；运营的；可投入使用的；操作层面的；（军事）作战的
definition_en: relating to the way something works in practice, or to the activities and costs of running an organization or machine
core_image: 一条生产线正在运转，指示灯全绿，工人各就各位，没有一处停着等修。
scene: 项目经理说系统已经通过测试，下周可以交给值班团队试用。 The system will be operational next week.
sceneCN: 这里 operational 是“已具备运行条件、可投入使用”（第 2 个义项）；句意：系统下周就可以投入运行；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 运行的；运营的；可投入使用的；操作层面的；（军事）作战的

senses.title: Relating to how it runs
senses.titleCN: 运行上的：与机器怎么转有关
senses.definition: relating to the working of a machine, system, or process
senses.definitionCN: 与机器、系统或流程如何运转有关
senses.example: The engineers separated design problems from operational problems.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把设计问题与运行问题分开处理。
senses.why: The suffix -al points to a domain: what happens while the thing is running, as distinct from how it was designed.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 指向一个领域：事物运转时发生的事，与它如何被设计区分开来。

senses.title: Ready to be used
senses.titleCN: 可投入使用：不是图纸，是能跑的
senses.definition: in a state of being able to work or be used as intended
senses.definitionCN: 处于能够按预期工作或使用的状态
senses.example: The new control tower is operational after two years of testing.
senses.exampleCN: 新控制塔经过两年测试后已可投入使用。
senses.why: Here the word answers a readiness question: the thing is not merely complete on paper, it can actually perform its function.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词回答的是“就绪”问题：事物不只在纸面上完成，它真能履行职责。

senses.title: The cost of keeping it running
senses.titleCN: 运营成本：让它每天转起来的钱
senses.definition: describing the expenses of running an organization or facility rather than building it
senses.definitionCN: 指维持组织或设施日常运转的开支，而非建设开支
senses.example: Operational costs rose with fuel and staff wages.
senses.exampleCN: 运营成本随燃料与员工工资上涨。
senses.why: Budgets split capital from operation: one pays to build, the other pays to keep the thing alive each day.
senses.whyCN: 预算把资本支出与运营支出分开：一笔付建设，另一笔付让它每天活下去。

senses.title: Defined by what you do
senses.titleCN: 操作定义：用做法代替概念
senses.definition: describing a definition that specifies the procedures or measurements used to identify something
senses.definitionCN: 指用识别某事物所需的具体程序或测量来下定义
senses.example: The study operationalised 'stress' as a rise in heart rate during the task.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究把“压力”操作化为任务期间心率上升。
senses.why: Some ideas cannot be seen directly, so science defines them by the operations that produce them, making the concept testable.
senses.whyCN: 有些概念无法直接看见，科学便用产生它的操作来定义，使概念可被检验。

senses.title: The mathematics of decisions
senses.titleCN: 运筹：把调度问题算清楚
senses.definition: describing the use of mathematical methods to improve the planning and running of complex activities
senses.definitionCN: 指用数学方法改进复杂活动的计划与运行
senses.example: Operational research cut the average waiting time at the depot.
senses.exampleCN: 运筹研究缩短了车站的平均等待时间。
senses.why: When an organization runs, its choices can be modelled; operational research treats scheduling as a problem with a best answer.
senses.whyCN: 组织一旦运转，其选择就可以建模型；运筹研究把调度当作一个有最优解的问题。

senses.title: At the level of action
senses.titleCN: 作战层面：战略之下、战术之上
senses.definition: describing the level of military activity concerned with planning and conducting campaigns
senses.definitionCN: 指军事活动中负责筹划与实施战役的层级
senses.example: Operational command decided where the units would meet before the battle.
senses.exampleCN: 作战指挥决定各部队在战斗前于何处会合。
senses.why: Military theory separates strategy (why to fight), operations (where and when to move), and tactics (how to fight the next hour).
senses.whyCN: 军事理论把战略（为何打）、作战（何时何地调动）与战术（接下来一小时怎么打）分开。

senses.title: Risk from daily running
senses.titleCN: 运营风险：不是市场，而是流程出错
senses.definition: describing the risk of loss from failed processes, people, systems, or external events
senses.definitionCN: 指因流程、人员、系统失效或外部事件造成损失的风险
senses.example: The bank holds capital against operational risk as well as credit risk.
senses.exampleCN: 银行不仅为信用风险，也为运营风险持有资本。
senses.why: Finance distinguishes risk from markets and borrowers from risk that arises simply because an organization must run every day.
senses.whyCN: 金融业把市场与借款人的风险，同“组织每天必须运转”本身带来的风险区分开。

senses.title: A circuit that computes
senses.titleCN: 运算放大器：让电路做算术
senses.definition: describing an amplifier designed to perform mathematical operations on signals
senses.definitionCN: 指为对信号执行数学运算而设计的放大器
senses.example: The operational amplifier summed the two sensor voltages.
senses.exampleCN: 运算放大器把两个传感器的电压相加。
senses.why: Early analogue computers used amplifiers to add and integrate; the name stayed even after the circuits became general-purpose components.
senses.whyCN: 早期模拟计算机用放大器做加法与积分；即使这些电路后来成了通用元件，名字仍保留下来。

intro.en: Operational is operation plus -al. Operation comes from Latin operatio, a working, from operari, to work, and opus, work.
intro.cn: operational 是 operation 加 -al。operation 来自拉丁语 operatio“劳作”，出自 operari“工作”与 opus“工作、作品”。

items.en: Opus meant work, a task, or a product of work. It survives in magnum opus and in the musical term opera.
items.cn: opus 意为工作、任务或劳动成果。它留在 magnum opus 与音乐术语 opera 中。

items.en: The verb meant to work, to labour, and to perform a task. It could describe both physical labour and the working of a power.
items.cn: 该动词意为工作、劳作、执行任务，既可描述体力劳动，也可描述某种力量的作用。

items.en: The noun named a working or an effect produced. Medieval Latin also used it for mathematical and medical procedures.
items.cn: 该名词指劳作或产生的效果。中世纪拉丁语也用它指数学与医学操作。

items.en: French operation covered work, a surgical procedure, and a military action. English borrowed all three.
items.cn: 法语 operation 涵盖工作、外科手术与军事行动；英语把这三层都借了进来。

items.en: Operational first meant 'of an operation' in surgery and mathematics, then extended to machines and organizations in the industrial age.
items.cn: operational 最初指外科与数学意义上的“操作的”， industrial 时代扩展到机器与组织。

items.en: The 20th century added operational research, operational definition, operational risk, and the operational amplifier.
items.cn: 20 世纪增加了运筹研究、操作定义、运营风险与运算放大器等用法。

note.en: The first group is the operate family; the second compares adjectives that describe readiness, function, and practical work.
note.cn: 第一组是 operate 词族；第二组比较表示就绪、功能与实际运作的形容词。

entries.definition: to work or control a machine, to run a business, or to perform surgery.
entries.definitionCN: 操作或控制机器、经营业务，或施行手术。

entries.definition: the act of working, a surgical procedure, or a military action.
entries.definitionCN: 工作行为、外科手术，或军事行动。

entries.definition: a person who runs a machine, or a company that runs a service.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器的人，或经营某项服务的公司。

entries.definition: working as designed. It stresses purpose served, while operational can also stress the running process or its cost.
entries.definitionCN: 按设计正常工作；强调所服务的目的，而 operational 也可强调运行过程或成本。

entries.definition: useful in real situations rather than theoretical. It judges usefulness, not running status.
entries.definitionCN: 在真实情境中有用而非理论的；判断的是用处，不是运行状态。

entries.definition: in action or in effect. A system can be active without being fully operational.
entries.definitionCN: 正在行动或生效的；系统可以处于活动状态却尚未完全可运行。

entries.definition: relating to long-term aims. In military theory it is the level above operational.
entries.definitionCN: 与长期目标有关；在军事理论中位于“作战”之上。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: opus, work, plus operari, to work, then -ation and -al. Operational means 'of the working'.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：opus“工作”，加 operari“工作”，再加 -ation 与 -al。operational 就是“属于运转的”。

normal.en: Opus is work; operational is the adjective of work being done right now.
normal.cn: opus 是工作；operational 是“工作正在进行”的形容词。

normal.en: Design is the drawing; operational is the machine actually turning.
normal.cn: 设计是图纸；operational 是机器真的在转。

normal.en: Operational costs are the money paid every day, not the money paid to build.
normal.cn: 运营成本是每天都要付的钱，不是建造时付的钱。

normal.en: An operational definition says what you do, not what you mean.
normal.cn: 操作定义说的是你怎么做，而不是你指什么。

normal.en: All green lights mean the system is operational.
normal.cn: 指示灯全绿，就表示系统处于可运行状态。

abstract.en: 'Operational' is where plans meet friction: everything works on paper, and only some things work at three in the morning.
abstract.cn: operational 是计划撞上摩擦的地方：纸面上一切都能行，凌晨三点只有一部分真能行。

abstract.en: An operational definition trades depth for testability, and the trade is usually worth making.
abstract.cn: 操作定义用深度换可检验性，这笔交易通常值得。

abstract.en: The word hides the labour inside the system; what looks automatic is a schedule of people and maintenance.
abstract.cn: 这个词把系统里的劳动藏了起来；看似自动的东西，其实是一张排班表与维护表。

examples.en: The plant became fully operational only after the cooling system passed its safety test.
examples.cn: 冷却系统通过安全测试后，这座工厂才全面投入运行。

examples.en: Operational costs, not construction costs, decide whether the railway survives.
examples.cn: 决定这条铁路能否存续的是运营成本，而不是建设成本。

examples.en: The team agreed on an operational definition of 'success' before collecting any data.
examples.cn: 团队在收集数据之前先就“成功”的操作定义达成一致。

dict_mnemonic.text: operate（运行）+ ional（的）——能跑起来、正在运转的，都是 operational。

root: 由 operation（运行、操作，源自拉丁语 operatio“劳作”）加 -al 构成；词基为拉丁语 opus“工作”与 operari“工作”，故本义为“与运转、操作有关的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of operational, all concerned with work being done. The work may be a machine turning, a system ready to run, the cost of daily upkeep, a procedure that defines a concept, a mathematical plan, a military campaign, a process failure, or an analogue computation.
sensesIntro.cn: operational 的八个义项都与“正在做的工作”有关。这工作可以是机器转动、系统就绪、日常维护成本、定义概念的程序、数学调度、军事战役、流程失效，或模拟电路运算。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a production line running with every indicator green and nobody waiting for a repair.
core.cn: 核心意象：生产线正在运转，指示灯全绿，没有人等着维修。

chain: ENGLISH OPERATION THE ACT OF RUNNING
OPERATIONAL OF RUNNING OR READY TO RUN

branches.en: RUNNING AND READY: the process of working, and the state of being fit to work.
branches.cn: 运转与就绪：工作的过程，以及能够工作的状态。

branches.en: THE PRICE OF RUNNING: daily costs and the risks that arise from ordinary processes.
branches.cn: 运转的代价：日常成本，以及普通流程带来的风险。

branches.en: DEFINITION BY PROCEDURE: a concept replaced by the operations that measure it.
branches.cn: 以程序定义：用测量它的操作取代概念本身。

branches.en: PLANNING ACTION: mathematical scheduling and the military level between strategy and tactics.
branches.cn: 筹划行动：数学调度，以及位于战略与战术之间的军事层级。

branches.en: COMPUTING BY CIRCUIT: an amplifier named for the operations it performs.
branches.cn: 用电路运算：因执行运算而得名的放大器。

intro.en: Operational is operation plus -al. The family runs through operate, operator, and operation, with opus as the Latin base.
intro.cn: operational 是 operation 加 -al。词族包括 operate、operator、operation，拉丁词基为 opus。

latinIntro.en: The base is opus, work, and its verb operari. Latin operatio names the working or the effect produced.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 opus“工作”及其动词 operari。拉丁语 operatio 指劳作或产生的效果。

items.meaning: to work, control, or carry out an activity
items.example: Only trained staff may operate the crane.
items.exampleCN: 只有受过训练的员工可以操作这台起重机。

items.meaning: the act of working, or a planned action
items.meaningCN: 工作行为，或计划好的行动
items.example: The operation runs from six in the morning.
items.exampleCN: 这项作业从早晨六点开始运行。

items.meaning: relating to running, or ready to run
items.meaningCN: 与运行有关的，或已可运行的
items.example: The system is operational but not yet open to the public.
items.exampleCN: 系统已可运行，但尚未向公众开放。

items.meaning: from the point of view of running
items.example: Operationally, the two designs are almost the same.
items.exampleCN: 从运行角度看，两种设计几乎一样。

items.meaning: a person or firm that runs something
items.meaningCN: 操作者，或经营某项业务的公司
items.example: The operator stopped the line for a safety check.
items.exampleCN: 操作员为安全检查停下了生产线。

items.meaning: to work together toward a shared aim
items.meaningCN: 为共同目标一起工作；合作
items.example: The two labs cooperated on the trial.
items.exampleCN: 两个实验室在该试验上合作。

items.meaning: in effect or ready to act; also a surgical adjective
items.meaningCN: 生效的、可行动的；也用于外科语境
items.example: The new rule is operative from January.

items.meaning: a work, especially a large artistic or musical work
items.meaningCN: 作品，尤指大型艺术或音乐作品
items.example: The symphony became his best-known opus.
items.exampleCN: 这部交响曲成了他最著名的作品。

items.meaning: able to be operated or used
items.example: The hatch is operable from inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个舱门可从内部操作。

definition_zh: 珍贵的；宝贵的；贵重的；值钱的；娇贵做作的；（precious little）少得可怜
definition_en: worth a great deal because of rarity, love or beauty; costly in material terms; over-refined in manner; and used before little or few to mean almost none
core_image: 掌心托着一枚旧顶针，金属已被磨得发亮
scene: 老人从抽屉最里层取出一只用手帕包着的小盒，盒里躺着一枚褪色的顶针。 She never wore the ring because it was too precious to risk losing.
sceneCN: 这里 precious 指「珍贵得不敢轻易动用」（第 1 个义项：因情感或稀有而宝贵）；句意为她从不戴那枚戒指，因为太珍贵，怕弄丢。图中可辨识物件：抽屉深处的手帕、褪色的顶针、磨亮的金属。

pos.zh: 珍贵的；宝贵的；贵重的；娇贵做作的

derivatives.zh: 由 precious 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「珍贵地；做作地」
由 precious 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「珍贵；矫饰」
由前缀 semi-（半）与 precious 复合而成，义为「半宝石的」

senses.title: Worth a great deal to someone
senses.definition: worth a great deal because it is rare, loved or impossible to replace
senses.definitionCN: 因稀有、被珍爱或无法替代而具有很大价值
senses.example: Her grandmother's letters are the most precious thing she owns.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母的信是她最珍视的东西。
senses.why: The Latin noun pretium named the value set on a thing, and its adjective pretiosus described whatever carried that value; English kept the worth and let the money side go.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 pretium 本指给一件东西定下的价值，形容词 pretiosus 就用来形容带着这份价值的东西；英语留下「价值」这一面，把「价钱」那一面让给了 price。

senses.title: Costly because of the material
senses.definition: made of a material that costs a lot, such as gold, silver or a fine stone
senses.definitionCN: 由金、银或上等宝石等昂贵材料制成
senses.example: The crown is set with precious stones brought from the east.
senses.exampleCN: 这顶王冠镶着从东方运来的宝石。
senses.why: A second step inside the same root: pretium also meant the money a thing costs, so the adjective could describe objects whose material alone makes them expensive, not only things loved for memory.
senses.whyCN: 同一词根的第二步：pretium 也能指一件东西所值的钱，于是这个形容词可以形容单凭材料就昂贵的物件，而不只是因回忆而被珍爱的东西。

senses.title: Over-refined in manner or style
senses.definition: too delicate, refined or fussy in behaviour, taste or style, so that it seems affected
senses.definitionCN: 举止、品味或风格过于精细挑剔，显得做作
senses.example: He has a precious way of holding his cup that amuses his friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他端杯子的样子讲究得有点做作，朋友们都拿这个打趣。
senses.why: Value set too high turns into a criticism: a person who treats small things as treasures is called precious in a mocking tone, so the word moves from the object to the attitude.
senses.whyCN: 把价值定得太高就会变成批评：一个把小事情当宝贝的人，会被带着讥讽地叫作 precious，词义于是从「物件」转到「态度」。

senses.title: Almost none, in precious little and precious few
senses.titleCN: （用于 precious little、precious few）少得可怜
senses.definition: used before little or few to stress that there is far less of something than is wanted
senses.definitionCN: 用在 little 或 few 前，强调某物的数量比所需少得多
senses.example: There is precious little time left before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 离截止只剩少得可怜的一点时间。
senses.why: This ironic use grows out of the same scale: a precious thing should be plentiful, so calling a tiny amount precious underlines how little of it there is.
senses.whyCN: 这种反讽用法长在同一杆价值尺度上：珍贵的东西本该充足，偏说那一点点很「珍贵」，反而把「少」强调出来。

intro.en: Precious and price are twins from one Latin noun, pretium. English sent price down the market road and precious down the road of worth, which is why the two now feel unrelated.
intro.cn: precious 与 price 是同一个拉丁名词 pretium 生下的一对双胞胎。英语让 price 走上买卖的路，让 precious 走上价值的另一条路，所以今天两者听起来毫不相干。

items.en: Pretium meant the price or value assigned to a thing, and it could name both the money paid and the worth people believed a thing had.
items.cn: pretium 指给一件东西定下的价钱或价值，既能指付出的钱，也能指人们认为它值多少。

items.en: Pretiosus was built on pretium and described something of great worth, especially costly stones, metals and cloth.
items.cn: pretiosus 由 pretium 构成，形容价值很高的东西，尤指昂贵的宝石、金属与织物。

items.en: Old French took the adjective as precios, meaning costly and highly valued, and passed it to English in the medieval period.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词写作 precios，意为昂贵的、极受重视的，并在中世纪传入英语。

items.en: Middle English precious kept the sense of great worth and began to be used for things valued for love rather than for money.
items.cn: 中古英语的 precious 保留「价值极高」的意思，并开始用于因感情而非金钱而宝贵的东西。

items.en: Modern English holds the split: price names what a thing costs, precious names what it is worth to someone, and the ironic precious little adds a third shade.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个分叉固定下来：price 指一件东西要多少钱，precious 指它对某人值多少，反讽的 precious little 又添了第三层色彩。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family that grew from Latin pretium; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for things people value.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语 pretium 长出来的同族词；近义组收人们用来形容「看重之物」的形容词。

entries.definition: The money a seller asks for something; it comes from the same Latin noun but took the commercial path.
entries.definitionCN: 卖方为一物索要的钱；与本词同出一个拉丁名词，但走的是买卖那条路。

entries.definition: To recognise the value of something, or to rise in value.
entries.definitionCN: 认识到某物的价值；也指升值。

entries.definition: A judgement of how much something is worth.
The quality of being precious, or of being over-refined.
entries.definitionCN: 珍贵的性质；也指做作讲究。

entries.definition: Worth a lot of money or of great use.
Expensive, or causing loss and damage.
entries.definitionCN: 昂贵的；也指造成损失和破坏的。

entries.definition: Loved and kept with care over a long time.
entries.definitionCN: 长期被珍爱、被小心保存的。

entries.definition: Much loved, and in British English also expensive.
entries.definitionCN: 深受喜爱的；英式英语里也指昂贵的。

normalIntro.en: One Latin noun of value splits into a market word and a word of worth; the English adjective then climbs from treasure to taste, and finally to irony.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示价值的拉丁名词分成了市场词与价值词；英语形容词再从珍宝爬到品味，最后落到反讽。

normal.en: Pretium gives both price and precious, so the twins are cousins: one counts coins, the other counts what the coins cannot buy.
normal.cn: pretium 同时生出 price 与 precious，这对双胞胎是表亲：一个数钱，一个数钱买不到的东西。

normal.en: Precious metal and precious stone are fixed phrases: the material itself is the value.
normal.cn: precious metal 与 precious stone 是固定搭配，材料本身就是价值。

normal.en: Precious little means very little, and the word is doing the opposite of its usual job there.
normal.cn: precious little 意为「少得可怜」，在这里这个词做的正好是它平常相反的事。

normal.en: Preciousness adds -ness to name the quality, and it can be praise or a complaint about fussiness.
normal.cn: preciousness 加 -ness 表示性质，既可以是称赞，也可以是在抱怨过于讲究。

normal.en: Semiprecious keeps semi-, half, for stones such as amethyst that are valued but not in the first rank.
normal.cn: semiprecious 保留 semi-（半）这个成分，用于紫水晶这类有价值但不算头等的宝石。

abstract.en: Value has two doors: what a thing costs and what a thing means, and English gave each door its own word.
abstract.cn: 价值有两扇门：一件东西值多少钱，以及它意味着什么；英语给每扇门配了一个词。

abstract.en: When the word is used as an insult, it is because caring too much about small refinements looks like a false scale of value.
abstract.cn: 这个词用来损人时，是因为过分在意细枝末节，看起来像一杆失准的价值秤。

abstract.en: Precious little is a small joke built into the language: the more precious the thing, the sharper the complaint that there is almost none.
abstract.cn: precious little 是语言里自带的一个小玩笑：东西越珍贵，抱怨「几乎没有」就越扎人。

examples.en: Her grandmother's letters are the most precious thing she owns.
examples.cn: 祖母的信是她最珍视的东西。

examples.en: The box was inlaid with precious stones.
examples.cn: 这只盒子镶着宝石。

examples.en: There is precious little evidence for that claim.
examples.cn: 那个说法几乎没有证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普雷舍斯」——贵重东西捧在手里，舍不得放下；precious 就是珍贵的。

root: 拉丁语 pretium（价钱、价值）→ 形容词 pretiosus（价值高的）→ 古法语 precios → 英语 precious。同族的 price 走的是「买卖价钱」那一路，precious 走的是「本身可贵」这一路，两者同源而语义分叉。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow one scale of value: a treasured thing, an expensive material, a fussy attitude that overvalues small things, and an ironic phrase that turns value into scarcity.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项沿着同一杆价值尺度展开：被珍爱之物、昂贵材料、把小节看得过重的做作，以及把「珍贵」翻成「稀缺」的反讽说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn thimble resting in an open palm, its metal polished by years of use.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚磨旧的顶针躺在摊开的手掌上，金属被多年使用磨得发亮。

branches.en: a ring kept in a handkerchief and never worn
branches.cn: 手帕里那枚从不戴的戒指

branches.en: stones prised out of a crown to be weighed
branches.cn: 从王冠上撬下、拿去称重的宝石

branches.en: one value measured by love and one by money
branches.cn: 一份价值用感情量，一份用钱量

branches.en: a cup lifted by the handle with two fingers
branches.cn: 用两根手指捏着杯柄端起的杯子

branches.en: a clock with almost no time left on it
branches.cn: 只剩一点点时间的钟

intro.en: A Latin noun of value, an adjective suffix that says full of it, and a French reshaping carry the word into English; -ly and -ness then build the adverb and the noun.
intro.cn: 一个表示价值的拉丁名词、一个表示「充满」的形容词后缀，以及法语的一次改写，把这个词带进英语；-ly 与 -ness 再分别造出副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Pretium and its adjective pretiosus are well recorded, and the verb appretiare valued a thing; English inherited the family through French.
latinIntro.cn: pretium 及其形容词 pretiosus 都有清楚的记录，动词 appretiare 意为「估价」；英语经法语继承了这一族词。

items.meaning: in a precious or affected way

definition_zh: 落后；滞后；时间间隔
definition_en: to fall behind others in movement or progress, or a delay between two events
core_image: 队伍前面的人已转过弯，最后一个还在原地系鞋带
scene: 操场上的队伍已经跑出半圈，最后一名选手才刚系好鞋带。 The oldest computer began to lag behind the others.
sceneCN: 这里是「落后、跟不上」（第 1 个义项：动词，指行动或进度落在别人后面）；句意为最旧的电脑开始落在其他电脑后面。图中可辨识物件：跑道、系鞋带的选手、远处的队伍。

derivatives.zh: 由 lag 双写 g 加 -ing 构成，义为「落后的；滞后」
由 lag 加 -ard 构成，义为「迟缓的人；落后者」

senses.title: To fall behind in movement or progress
senses.definition: to move or develop more slowly than others, so that a distance opens up
senses.definitionCN: 行动或发展比其他人慢，因而拉开距离
senses.example: The oldest computer began to lag behind the others.
senses.exampleCN: 最旧的电脑开始落在其他电脑后面。
senses.why: Lag probably imitates the sense of something dragging at the back; the word pictures a trailing end rather than a measured distance.
senses.whyCN: lag 很可能来自「拖在后面」的感觉，它描绘的是队尾，而不是量出来的距离。

senses.title: A delay between two connected events
senses.definition: the period of time by which one event follows another that should be simultaneous
senses.definitionCN: 两个本应同时的事件之间相隔的那段时间
senses.example: There is a slight time lag between the sound and the picture.
senses.exampleCN: 声音和画面之间有一点时间滞后。
senses.why: Once the verb names being behind, the noun can name the measurable gap itself, as in a time lag.
senses.whyCN: 动词既然表示「落在后面」，名词就能指那段可测量的差距，例如 time lag。

senses.title: The tiredness caused by crossing time zones
senses.definition: the bodily discomfort felt after a long flight across several time zones
senses.definitionCN: 跨越多个时区长途飞行后身体感到的不适
senses.example: It took him three days to get over his jet lag.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了三天才缓过时差反应。
senses.why: The body's internal clock lags behind local time after a flight, and the compound jet lag names exactly that lag.
senses.whyCN: 飞行之后，身体的生物钟落后于当地时间，jet lag 这个复合词正是把这种「滞后」说了出来。

intro.en: Lag is a word of uncertain origin, usually connected with Scandinavian forms for something dragging behind.
intro.cn: lag 来源不确定，通常与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「拖在后面」的形式相联系。

items.en: The earliest records do not settle whether lag came from Scandinavian or from an English dialect.
items.cn: 最早记录无法确定 lag 是来自斯堪的纳维亚语还是英格兰方言。

items.en: A related Swedish dialect verb for moving slowly or dragging is often cited, but the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 常被提到的是一个意义为「慢慢移动、拖」的瑞典方言动词，但确切形式并不确定。

items.en: Lag appears in English in the sixteenth century with the sense of trailing behind.
items.cn: lag 在十六世纪进入英语，意为「拖在后面」。

items.en: The noun and the modern technical sense of a time lag develop in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 名词用法以及 time lag 这一现代技术义在十九世纪发展出来。

items.en: Modern English adds jet lag and digital lag, keeping the same picture of something running behind.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上 jet lag 与 digital lag，仍保留「某物跑在后面」的画面。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that resemble lag in spelling; the near-meaning group collects words for delay and trailing behind.
note.cn: 形近组收与 lag 拼写相近的词；近义组收表示延迟、落后的词。

entries.definition: A piece of cloth used as a signal, or to become tired.
entries.definitionCN: 旗子；也可指「变得疲倦」；只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A small label attached to something.
Falling behind, or material used for insulation.
A period of waiting before something happens.
To be behind others in a race or competition.
A reduction in speed or activity.

normalIntro.en: The word is short, with a doubled g in its inflections, and its family stays close to the trailing end of a line.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词很短，变形时双写 g，同族词都贴近队伍末尾。

normal.en: Lag doubles its g before -ed and -ing: lagged, lagging.
normal.cn: lag 在 -ed、-ing 前双写 g：lagged、lagging。

normal.en: Lag behind is the common phrase for being slower than others.
normal.cn: lag behind 是表示「落在别人后面」的常用搭配。

normal.en: Time lag is the measurable gap between two events.
normal.cn: time lag 是两个事件之间可测量的间隔。

normal.en: Jet lag joins jet to lag for the tiredness after a flight.
normal.cn: jet lag 把 jet 与 lag 组合，指飞行后的疲倦。

normal.en: Laggard adds -ard, a suffix seen in words for people with a habit.
normal.cn: laggard 加 -ard，这个后缀常见于表示有某种习性的人。

abstract.en: A trailing end is not a fixed distance but a relation: someone must be ahead for lag to exist.
abstract.cn: 队尾不是固定距离而是一种关系：必须有人在前面，才有 lag。

abstract.en: The same word covers a runner, a machine and a body clock, because all three can run behind an expected pace.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能指跑步的人、机器和生物钟，因为三者都可能落后于预期节奏。

abstract.en: Lag turns difference in speed into something you can name and measure.
abstract.cn: lag 把速度上的差异变成可以命名、可以测量的东西。

examples.en: The oldest computer began to lag behind the others.
examples.cn: 最旧的电脑开始落在其他电脑后面。

examples.en: There is a slight time lag between the sound and the picture.
examples.cn: 声音和画面之间有一点时间滞后。

examples.en: It took him three days to get over his jet lag.
examples.cn: 他花了三天才缓过时差反应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赖格」——赖在格子里不肯往前走，就落后了；lag 记作「落后」。

root: 来源不确定，一般认为与斯堪的纳维亚语中表示「拖在后面」的方言动词有关，确切形式无法确认。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a trailing end; it extends from a person falling behind to a measurable time gap and to the body clock running late.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「拖在队尾」；由人落后扩展到可测量的时间差，再扩展到生物钟的错后。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last runner still tying a shoelace while the line turns the corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：队伍已经转过弯，最后一名还在系鞋带。

branches.en: a runner at the back of the pack
branches.cn: 跑在队伍最后的人

branches.en: a clock that is a few seconds slow
branches.cn: 慢了几秒的钟

branches.en: a traveller awake at the wrong hour
branches.cn: 在错误时间醒来的旅客

branches.en: the same backward pull, in legs and in seconds
branches.cn: 同一种向后拖的力量，表现在腿上和秒数上

branches.en: two screens showing the same scene a beat apart
branches.cn: 两块屏幕同一画面差了一拍

intro.en: There is no settled prefix or root here, so the family is built from the bare stem and two suffixes.
intro.cn: 这里没有确定的前缀或词根，同族词由光裸词干加两个后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 天文学
definition_en: the scientific study of the universe, stars, planets and other celestial bodies
core_image: 一张从地球轨道向外看去的银河全景图，星点密密麻麻
scene: 开学第一节课老师说： Astronomy asks what the universe is made of, how it began, and where it's going.
sceneCN: 这里指「研究宇宙和天体的科学」（第1个义项：科学学科）；句意为天文学追问宇宙由什么构成、如何起源、去往何处。

senses.title: The scientific discipline itself
senses.titleCN: 作为学科本身的天文学
senses.definition: one of the oldest natural sciences, studying everything outside Earth's atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 最古老的自然科学之一，研究地球大气层以外的一切
senses.example: Astronomy has reshaped our picture of the universe in the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 过去一百年里天文学重塑了我们对宇宙的认识。
senses.why: The Greek roots astron (star) + nomos (law) make this the 'law of stars'.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根 astron（星）+ nomos（法）让它成为「星辰之法」。

senses.title: Observational astronomy
senses.definition: the branch that gathers data with telescopes, cameras and detectors from the ground or space
senses.definitionCN: 用望远镜、相机和探测器从地面或太空收集数据的分支
senses.example: Observational astronomy got a new eye when the Hubble telescope launched in 1990.
senses.exampleCN: 1990 年哈勃升空给观测天文学添了一只新眼。
senses.why: Observational astronomy is the empirical side, gathering evidence that theorists use.
senses.whyCN: 观测天文学是经验的一面，收集理论家使用的证据。

senses.title: Theoretical astronomy
senses.definition: the branch that builds models to explain what observations reveal
senses.definitionCN: 建立模型解释观测结果的分支
senses.example: Theoretical astronomy predicts where black holes should lie in galaxy centres.
senses.exampleCN: 理论天文学预言黑洞应该在星系中心哪里。
senses.why: Theory gives meaning to observations, turning data into understanding.
senses.whyCN: 理论给观测赋予意义，把数据变成理解。

senses.title: Astronomy history and pre-scientific
senses.titleCN: 前科学的天文观测（历史上）
senses.definition: the ancient practice of tracking skies for calendars, religion or navigation, before the scientific method
senses.definitionCN: 科学方法出现之前，为历算、宗教或导航追踪天象的古老实践
senses.example: Maya astronomy predicted eclipses with remarkable accuracy without telescopes.
senses.exampleCN: 玛雅天文学不用望远镜就以惊人准确度预测了日食月食。
senses.why: Early astronomy blended with astrology, religion and agriculture.
senses.whyCN: 早期天文学与占星、宗教、农业混在一起。

senses.title: Popular astronomy / stargazing
senses.definition: the hobby or public outreach of observing the sky with small telescopes or the naked eye
senses.definitionCN: 用小望远镜或肉眼观星的爱好或科普活动
senses.example: The park hosts free astronomy nights every month for the public.
senses.exampleCN: 公园每月给公众办免费天文之夜。
senses.why: Popular astronomy shares the sky with non-scientists, keeping wonder alive.
senses.whyCN: 科普天文把星空分享给非科学家，让好奇心延续。

senses.title: Subfields: planetary, stellar, galactic
senses.definition: astronomy splits into subfields by object studied: planets, stars, galaxies, the universe as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 按研究对象划分的子学科：行星、恒星、星系、宇宙整体
senses.example: She chose galactic astronomy, studying how the Milky Way formed.
senses.exampleCN: 她选了星系天文学，研究银河系如何形成。
senses.why: Each subfield brings its own tools and questions, but all belong under the same root.
senses.whyCN: 每个子学科有自己的工具和问题，但都在同一词根之下。

senses.title: Astrology vs astronomy
senses.definition: astronomy is the scientific study; astrology uses celestial positions to predict human affairs and is not a science
senses.definitionCN: astronomy 是科学研究；占星用天体位置预言人类事务，不是科学
senses.example: Most universities offer astronomy, none offer astrology as a science.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数大学教 astronomy，没有哪所大学把占星作为科学开设。
senses.why: The -logy ending in astrology sounds scientific but does not mean it uses the scientific method.
senses.whyCN: astrology 里的 -logy 听起来科学但不代表它用科学方法。

senses.title: Influencing other sciences
senses.definition: astronomy overlaps with physics, chemistry, geology, biology and information science
senses.definitionCN: astronomy 与物理、化学、地质、生物、信息科学有交叉
senses.example: Discoveries in astronomy often drive new inventions in sensing and computing.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学的发现常常推动传感和计算的新发明。
senses.why: The universe is the largest laboratory; everything physical here is also physical 'out there'.
senses.whyCN: 宇宙是最大的实验室；这里一切物理事物在「外面」也是物理的。

intro.en: astronomy comes from Greek: astron 'star' + nomos 'law, custom' → 'the law of stars'; it arrived in Latin as astronomia and entered English around the 13th century.
intro.cn: astronomy 来自希腊语：astron「星」+ nomos「法」→「星辰之法」；经拉丁语 astronomia，13 世纪进入英语。

items.en: Aristotle used astronomia to mean the study of celestial motions; nomos meant 'the law that governs'.
items.cn: 亚里士多德用 astronomia 指对天体运动的研究；nomos 意为「支配之法」。

items.en: Latin borrowed astronomia directly from Greek, keeping both the word and the meaning.
items.cn: 拉丁语直接从希腊语借入 astronomia，词和意思都不变。

items.en: Middle English astronomie (13th century) was the standard spelling, borrowed through Old French astronomie.
items.cn: 中古英语 astronomie（13 世纪）是标准拼写，经古法语 astronomie 借入。

items.en: Spelling shifted to astronomy by the 16th century, matching the Greek -nomy suffix pattern.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪拼写变成 astronomy，对齐希腊 -nomy 后缀形式。

items.en: Copernicus and Kepler redefined astronomy in the 16th and 17th centuries as mathematical physics of the heavens.
items.cn: 哥白尼和开普勒在 16-17 世纪把 astronomy 重新定义为天上的数学物理。

items.en: Today astronomy spans from subatomic particles to the structure of the cosmos.
items.cn: 今天 astronomy 从亚原子粒子延伸到宇宙结构。

note.en: Group one holds astronomy-derived words; group two holds related 'sky science' and related -nomy / -logy terms.
note.cn: 第一组是 astronomy 派生的词；第二组是相关的「天空科学」和相近的 -nomy / -logy 术语。

entries.definition: A person who works in astronomy.
Of astronomy; informally, huge in size.
entries.definitionCN: 天文学的；口语里表示「极大的」。

entries.definition: Physics applied to astronomical objects; technically a subfield.
entries.definitionCN: 用物理研究天体；严格说是 astronomy 的子学科。

entries.definition: The study of life in the universe; also called exobiology.
entries.definitionCN: 研究宇宙中的生命；也叫 exobiology。

entries.definition: Not a science; uses celestial positions to interpret human affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 非科学；用天体位置解读人类事务。

entries.definition: The part of astronomy that studies the origin and structure of the whole universe.
entries.definitionCN: 研究整个宇宙起源和结构的 astronomy 分支。

entries.definition: The specific study of how the universe began; narrower than cosmology.
entries.definitionCN: 专门研究宇宙如何起源；范围比 cosmology 窄。

entries.definition: Describing and mapping the universe rather than modelling its physics.
entries.definitionCN: 描述和绘制宇宙，而非建模其物理。

normalIntro.en: astron- = star, -nomy = law → astronomy = the law of stars.
normalIntro.cn: astron- = 星，-nomy = 法 → astronomy = 星辰之法。

normal.en: astron (Greek for star) + nomos (Greek for law) = astronomy.
normal.cn: astron（希腊语「星」）+ nomos（希腊语「法」）= astronomy。

normal.en: An astronomer follows the laws of stars.
normal.cn: 天文学家追随星辰之法。

normal.en: People once called astronomy 'the science of the stars'.
normal.cn: 人们曾经把 astronomy 叫「星辰的科学」。

normal.en: Astronomy uses telescopes; astrology uses horoscopes.
normal.cn: Astronomy 用望远镜；占星用星盘。

normal.en: Kepler wrote the laws of planetary motion — laws of stars.
normal.cn: 开普勒写了行星运动定律——星辰之法。

abstract.en: A clear night, the Milky Way overhead, a telescope pointing somewhere deep.
abstract.cn: 晴朗的夜，头顶银河，望远镜指向深处某处。

abstract.en: A thousand-year quest to figure out where we are and why.
abstract.cn: 一场绵延千年的追问：我们在哪、为什么。

abstract.en: Something ancient, vast, and always pointing up.
abstract.cn: 一种古老、浩瀚、永远向上指的东西。

examples.en: Radio astronomy began in the 1930s when engineers accidentally picked up cosmic radio noise.
examples.cn: 射电天文学始于 1930 年代，工程师无意中接收到宇宙射电噪声。

examples.en: Astronomy is a team science; modern observations involve telescopes on every continent and in space.
examples.cn: astronomy 是团队科学；现代观测涉及每个大陆和太空的望远镜。

examples.en: Her PhD combined astronomy with statistics to hunt for exoplanets.
examples.cn: 她的博士结合了天文学和统计来寻找系外行星。

dict_mnemonic.text: astron-（星）+ -nomy（法）= 星辰之法 = 天文学

root: astron（希腊语，星）+ nomos（法）→ astronomia → astronomy。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses map the many ways we study the sky: observing, theorising, history, popular enthusiasm, subfields, distinguishing from astrology, and influence on other sciences.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项覆盖我们研究天空的种种方式：观测、理论、历史、业余爱好、子学科、与占星区分、对其他科学的影响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a telescope pointed at a dark sky, pulling faint stars into bright focus.
core.cn: 核心意象：指向暗空的望远镜，把暗淡的星辰拉成清晰的焦点。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND OBSERVATION: the field itself, plus the work of watching and measuring the sky.
branches.cn: 学科与观测：这门学科本身，以及观测测量天空的工作。

branches.en: THEORETICAL: the branch that builds models and predictions.
branches.cn: 理论：负责建立模型与预言的分支。

branches.en: HISTORICAL: pre-scientific sky watching and its records.
branches.cn: 历史：前科学时期的天象观测及其记录。

branches.en: POPULAR / OUTREACH: amateur stargazing and public explanation.
branches.cn: 科普 / 业余：业余观星与面向公众的解释。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION / BOUNDARIES / INFLUENCE: subfields, the line against astrology, and effects on other sciences.
branches.cn: 分类 / 边界 / 影响：子学科、与占星的界线，以及对其他学科的影响。

intro.en: astronomy is built from Greek astron 'star' plus the Greek suffix -nomy 'law, system of rules'; many astronomy words share astron-.

latinIntro.en: astron is purely Greek, not Latin; the Latin 'star' is stella, which gives stellar.
