definition_zh: 魅力；吸引力；护身符；使着迷
definition_en: the quality of pleasing and attracting people, a small object worn for luck, or to delight someone greatly
core_image: 一句低唱的咒语让人不由自主地靠近
scene: 老人讲起年轻时的故事，满屋人都安静了。 His easy charm made the room fall silent.
sceneCN: 这里 charm 指「魅力」（第 1 个义项：吸引人的力量）；句意是他从容的魅力让满屋人安静下来。

senses.title: The power to please
senses.definition: the quality of pleasing and attracting other people
senses.definitionCN: 讨人喜欢、吸引他人的品质
senses.example: His easy charm made the room fall silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他从容的魅力让满屋人安静下来。
senses.why: A charm was first a sung spell, and the pull of a spell became the pull of a personality.
senses.whyCN: charm 最初是唱出的咒语，咒语的牵引力变成了人格的吸引力。

senses.title: A small lucky object
senses.definition: a small object worn to bring good luck or keep harm away
senses.definitionCN: 佩戴以求好运或驱除伤害的小物件
senses.example: She wore a silver charm on her wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 她手腕上戴着一枚银质护身符。
senses.why: The spell shrank into a small object that was believed to carry its power.
senses.whyCN: 咒语缩小成一件被认为携带其力量的小物件。

senses.title: To delight someone
senses.definition: to please or attract someone strongly
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地取悦或吸引某人
senses.example: The old town charmed every visitor.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城让每位游客着迷。
senses.why: Bewitching a person with a song became bewitching them with delight.
senses.whyCN: 用歌声迷惑一个人，变成了用愉悦迷住一个人。

intro.en: Charm began as a Latin word for a song, especially a sung spell, and only later meant personal appeal.
intro.cn: charm 起初是拉丁语中「歌」的说法，尤指唱出的咒语，后来才指个人吸引力。

items.en: Carmen meant a song, poem or incantation.
items.cn: 拉丁语 carmen 意为歌、诗或咒语。

items.en: Charme named a magic spell and the words that carried it.
items.cn: charme 指魔法咒语以及承载它的词句。

items.en: English charm first meant an enchantment or a magic formula.
items.cn: 英语 charm 先指魔法或咒文。

items.en: The word extended to a small object worn for luck.
items.cn: 该词扩展到为求好运而佩戴的小物件。

items.en: The word now chiefly means personal attractiveness and the act of delighting.
items.cn: 如今该词主要指个人吸引力与使人愉悦的行为。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the charm stem, while the meaning group lists appeal and magic words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 charm 词干，近义组列出吸引力与魔法类词。

entries.definition: very pleasing and attractive
a person who charms others
without attractiveness
the power to interest people
a quality that draws people near
a small object worn for protection
entries.definitionCN: 为护身而佩戴的小物件

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the song root, the lucky object and the phrase work like a charm.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「歌」词根、幸运物件以及短语 work like a charm。

normal.en: Charm and carol both begin with a Latin song, though only charm kept the magic.
normal.cn: charm 与 carol 都源自拉丁语的歌，但只有 charm 保留了魔法。

normal.en: A good luck charm is a spell shrunk to pocket size.
normal.cn: good luck charm 是缩到口袋大小的咒语。

normal.en: Work like a charm means the method succeeds as if by magic.
normal.cn: work like a charm 意为方法像施了魔法般奏效。

normal.en: Charm the audience shifts the word from object to action.
normal.cn: charm the audience 把这个词从物件转为动作。

normal.en: The adjective charming drops the e and adds -ing.
normal.cn: 形容词 charming 去掉 e 再加 -ing。

abstract.en: Picture an old singer humming a spell over a sleeping child.
abstract.cn: 想象一位老歌者对着熟睡的孩子低唱咒语。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny silver fish swinging on a bracelet.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小银鱼在手链上晃动。

abstract.en: Picture a whole room turning quiet at one voice.
abstract.cn: 想象整个房间因一个声音而安静下来。

examples.en: The village has a charm that cities lose.
examples.cn: 这个村庄有一种城市已经失去的魅力。

examples.en: He kept his mother's charm in his pocket.
examples.cn: 他把母亲的护身符放在口袋里。

examples.en: The children were charmed by the puppet show.
examples.cn: 孩子们被木偶戏迷住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: charm 原义是「歌」：一首咒歌让人着迷，后来就指一个人身上的魅力。

root: 源自拉丁语 carmen（歌、咒语），经古法语 charme 进入英语；由「咒语」引申为护身符、魅力与使人着迷。

sensesIntro.en: A sung spell gives an object its luck, a personality its pull and a verb its power to delight.
sensesIntro.cn: 唱出的咒语给物件以好运，给性格以吸引力，也给动词以使人愉悦的力量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spell that pulls a person closer.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一个人拉近的咒语。

branches.en: Personal charm is the spell without words.
branches.cn: 个人魅力是不用念出的咒语。

branches.en: A charm on a bracelet carries the old magic.
branches.cn: 手链上的护身符携带古老的魔法。

branches.en: To charm is to cast that spell on someone.
branches.cn: 使着迷就是把这道咒语施于人。

branches.en: The noun names the pull, the verb performs it.
branches.cn: 名词指那股牵引力，动词则施展它。

branches.en: Object and action both come from the spell.
branches.cn: 物件与动作都来自那道咒语。

intro.en: Charm forms charming, charmer and charmless with common endings.
intro.cn: charm 借助常见词尾构成 charming、charmer 与 charmless。

latinIntro.en: Latin carmen is the song or spell that stands behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carmen 是英语这个词背后的歌或咒语。

items.example: The charms hung on a chain.
They were charmed by the town.
items.exampleCN: 他们被这座小镇迷住了。

latinEntries.exampleCN: charme 以 charm 进入英语。

definition_zh: 无限的；无穷的；极大的
definition_en: without limits or end in space, time or number
core_image: 一条向两端延伸到看不见尽头的直线
scene: 夜里抬头看天，星星数也数不完。 The night sky seemed infinite to the child.
sceneCN: 这里 infinite 是「无限的」（第 1 个义项：没有边界或尽头）；句意是那片夜空在孩子看来是无限的。

pos.zh: 形容词：无限的；无穷的；极大的

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ity，义为「无限；无穷」
去掉否定前缀，义为「有限的」
同出拉丁 finis，义为「不定式」

senses.title: Without end in space
senses.definition: having no boundary, so that it cannot be crossed
senses.definitionCN: 没有边界，无法穿越
senses.example: Space is thought to be infinite, or at least very large.
senses.exampleCN: 空间被认为是无限的，或者至少极大。
senses.why: In- means not and finis means end, so the word is literally endless.
senses.whyCN: in- 表示不，finis 表示终点，所以这个词字面就是没有尽头。

senses.title: Without end in number
senses.definition: too many to be counted, or continuing without a last term
senses.definitionCN: 多得无法计数，或没有最后一项
senses.example: There are infinitely many numbers between one and two.
senses.exampleCN: 一与二之间有无限多个数。
senses.why: Mathematics turns the image of endless space into endless counting.
senses.whyCN: 数学把无尽空间的画面变成了无尽的计数。

senses.title: Without limit in degree
senses.definition: having no measurable limit, often used as a strong intensifier
senses.definitionCN: 没有可衡量的限度，常作很强的加强语
senses.example: You need infinite patience to teach small children.
senses.exampleCN: 教小孩子需要无限的耐心。
senses.why: Everyday speech borrows the word for anything that feels beyond measure.
senses.whyCN: 日常语言把这词借给任何感觉无法计量的东西。

senses.title: The boundless whole
senses.definition: what has no limits, used with the in philosophy
senses.definitionCN: 哲学中与 the 连用，指没有限度者
senses.example: The mystics spoke of union with the infinite.
senses.exampleCN: 神秘主义者谈到与无限合一。
senses.why: An adjective with the becomes an abstract noun for the whole of what is endless.
senses.whyCN: 形容词与 the 连用，成为指无尽整体的抽象名词。

senses.title: Endless in time
senses.definition: going on forever, with no end in time
senses.definitionCN: 永远持续，在时间上没有终点
senses.example: They imagined an infinite series of past days.
senses.exampleCN: 他们想象过去的日子是无限的系列。
senses.why: From space the word stretches to time, another kind of extent.
senses.whyCN: 从空间出发，这个词延伸到时间，这是另一种广延。

intro.en: Infinite joins Latin in-, not, to finitus, finished, from finis, end or boundary.
intro.cn: infinite 把拉丁否定 in- 加到 finitus（已结束的）上，后者出自 finis（终点、边界）。

items.en: Finis meant a boundary or end, as in the finish of a race.
items.cn: finis 意为边界或终点，如赛跑的终点。

items.en: Finitus, finished or limited, took the negative prefix to give infinitus.
items.cn: finitus（已结束的、有限的）加否定前缀，得到 infinitus。

items.en: The word entered English through French in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Theology first used infinite of God, then mathematics took it over.
items.cn: 神学先用 infinite 形容上帝，随后数学接管了它。

items.en: The loose sense of very great became common in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 「极大」这一宽松义项在日常口语中普遍起来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the finis family; the near-meaning group holds words for what has no limit.
note.cn: 形近组收 finis 词族；近义组收表示无边无际的词。

entries.definition: The state of having no limit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无限」，是本词的名词。

entries.definition: Having limits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有限的」，去掉否定前缀。

entries.definition: To state the exact meaning, to set limits.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「下定义」，本义是划定边界。

entries.definition: Having no end.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无尽的」，最直白的说法。

entries.definition: Without limits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无边无际的」。

entries.definition: Without any limit.

normalIntro.en: The hooks lock onto finis, the negative prefix and the mathematical picture of a number line.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子抓住 finis、否定前缀以及数轴的数学画面。

normal.en: In- means not, finis means end, so infinite is simply not ended.
normal.cn: in- 表示不，finis 表示终点，所以 infinite 就是没有终点。

normal.en: The same root gives finish, define and final: all about limits.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 finish、define、final，都与界限有关。

normal.en: Infinity is the noun, infinitely the adverb, finite the opposite.
normal.cn: infinity 是名词，infinitely 是副词，finite 是反义词。

normal.en: The infinity sign looks like a line with no end, the word made visible.
normal.cn: 无穷符号像一条没有尽头的线，是这个词的可见形式。

normal.en: Infinite patience is figurative, but the picture is still an endless length.
normal.cn: infinite patience 是比喻，但画面仍是一段无尽的长度。

abstract.en: Infinite is not a big number; it is the absence of a last one.
abstract.cn: infinite 不是一个大数，而是缺少那最后一个数。

abstract.en: A boundary is what finis means, so to be infinite is to be beyond all drawing of lines.
abstract.cn: finis 的意思是边界，所以无限就是超出一切划界。

abstract.en: The word makes the mind stretch until it can no longer finish the picture.
abstract.cn: 这个词让头脑不断延展，直到画不完那个画面。

examples.en: The universe may be finite or infinite; nobody knows.
examples.cn: 宇宙可能是有限的，也可能是无限的，无人知晓。

examples.en: She showed infinite patience with the new students.
examples.cn: 她对新来的学生表现出无限的耐心。

examples.en: An infinite series has no last term.
examples.cn: 无限级数没有最后一项。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因飞你特」——因为飞得特别远，才显得无穷无尽。

root: 拉丁否定前缀 in-（不）+ finitus（有限的），出自 finis（终点、边界）；同族词有 infinity、finite、define。

sensesIntro.en: From the literal absence of a boundary, infinite moves to endless counting, then to immeasurable degree, to the philosophical whole and to time without end.
sensesIntro.cn: 从字面上没有边界出发，infinite 走向无尽的计数，再到无法计量的程度、哲学上的整体，以及没有终点的时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line running past both edges of the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条直线越过纸的两端。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: no edge can be reached.
branches.cn: 空间线：到不了任何边缘。

branches.en: NUMBER LINE: counting never stops.
branches.cn: 数量线：计数永不停止。

branches.en: DEGREE LINE: patience without measure.
branches.cn: 程度线：无法计量的耐心。

branches.en: WHOLE LINE: the infinite as a noun.
branches.cn: 整体线：作为名词的「无限」。

branches.en: TIME LINE: extent stretched into duration.
branches.cn: 时间线：广延拉长为持续。

intro.en: A negative prefix on an adjective of limits, the same formula behind countless English words.
intro.cn: 一个在「有限」形容词前的否定前缀，这一构式造出无数英语词。

latinIntro.en: The root finis, end, appears in final, finish, define and confine.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 finis（终点）见于 final、finish、define 与 confine。

definition_zh: 挑衅；激怒；激怒的原因；煽动
definition_en: the act of deliberately making someone angry, or something that stirs a person into reacting
core_image: 有人探身向前，把一根手指点到别人眼前，等着对方跳起来
scene: 酒馆里，一个陌生人故意把椅子撞到旁边那桌，又笑着退回自己的位置，等着看对方怎么反应。 He hit back only after repeated provocation and was later judged less harshly.
sceneCN: 这里取「挑衅、激怒」的意思（第 1 个义项：故意惹人发怒的行为）；句意为他在屡次受到挑衅之后才还手，后来因此被从轻看待。陌生人撞椅子的那个动作就是线索。

pos.zh: 挑衅；激怒；激怒的原因；煽动

derivatives.zh: 与 provocation 同出拉丁语 provocare（把人唤出来），义为「激怒；引起」
由拉丁词干 provocat- 加 -ive 构成，义为「挑衅的；煽动性的」
由 provocative 加 -ly 构成，义为「挑衅地」
借自法语，指受雇挑起事端的人，如 agent provocateur

senses.title: The act of deliberately making someone angry
senses.definition: the act of saying or doing something on purpose to make someone angry or to make them react
senses.definitionCN: 故意说或做某事，使某人生气或作出反应的行为
senses.example: He lashed out at the reporter without any provocation.
senses.exampleCN: 他在没有受到任何挑衅的情况下对那名记者发作。
senses.why: Latin provocare meant to call someone forth, like a challenge shouted across a space, so the noun starts as an invitation to fight rather than as an emotion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 provocare 意为「把人叫出来」，像隔着一段距离发出的挑战，所以这个名词的起点是「邀人来战」，而不是某种情绪。

senses.title: Something that causes anger or a reaction
senses.definition: an event or remark that stirs someone into anger or into action
senses.definitionCN: 激起某人愤怒或促使其行动的某个事件或言语
senses.example: The insult was the provocation that started the whole quarrel.
senses.exampleCN: 那句侮辱就是引起整场争吵的导火索。
senses.why: If the word names the calling forth, it easily slides to the thing that does the calling: what was an act becomes a cause standing in front of the reaction.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词指「把人叫出来」这件事，就很容易滑到「发出呼唤的那个东西」：原本是一个动作，变成了立在反应之前的起因。

senses.title: Behaviour that reduces blame in law
senses.definition: in law, words or actions that make an ordinary person lose self-control and are therefore weighed when judging the response
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指使常人失去自制的言语或行为，判断回应是否过当时会予以考虑
senses.example: The defence argued that the killing followed severe provocation.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方主张，那起杀人是在受到严重激惹之后发生的。
senses.why: Courts need a name for the pressure that pushes a person past the limit, and this noun supplies it, which is why the word can lighten a sentence while naming no act of the accused.
senses.whyCN: 法庭需要为那种把人逼过界限的压力起个名字，这个名词正好提供；所以它能减轻刑罚，却并不指被告自己的任何动作。

intro.en: Provocation comes from a Latin verb that meant to call someone forth, built from pro-, forward, and vocare, to call; it is unrelated to provide and province.
intro.cn: provocation 来自一个意为「把人叫出来」的拉丁语动词，由 pro-（向前）与 vocare（呼喊）构成；它与 provide、province 都不同源。

items.en: Vocare meant to call, and it is the calling root behind a large Latin family.
items.cn: vocare 意为呼喊，是拉丁语中一大族词背后那个「叫」的词根。

items.en: With pro-, forward, provocare meant to call someone out, to challenge or to stir them to action.
items.cn: 加上表示向前的 pro-，provocare 意为把人叫出来、挑战他或促使他行动。

items.en: The noun provocatio named a calling forth, and in Roman law also a formal appeal against a decision.
items.cn: 名词 provocatio 指「唤出」，在罗马法中也指对裁决的正式上诉。

items.en: Old French borrowed the noun as provocation and narrowed it towards the stirring of anger.
items.cn: 古法语借入该名词作 provocation，并把它收窄到「激起怒气」这一方向。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun for the act, for the thing that triggers it, and for the legal pressure that explains a reaction.
items.cn: 现代英语保留这个名词，用来指行为本身、触发它的东西，以及法律上能解释某种反应的压力。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin verb of calling out; the near-meaning group gathers words for acts and remarks that sting.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「喊出来」动词上的词；近义组收表示刺伤人的举动与言语的词。

entries.definition: To make someone angry or to stir something up.
Likely to annoy people or to stir thought and desire.
entries.definitionCN: 容易惹人恼火，或能激起思考与欲望的。

entries.definition: Someone paid to stir trouble, as in agent provocateur.
entries.definitionCN: 受雇挑起事端的人，如 agent provocateur。

entries.definition: To speak publicly in favour of something.
A remark or act meant to hurt someone's pride.
entries.definitionCN: 意在伤害他人自尊的言语或举动。

entries.definition: A remark made to mock and provoke someone.
entries.definitionCN: 用来嘲笑并激怒他人的话。

entries.definition: The act of urging someone to act, especially wrongly.
entries.definitionCN: 鼓动他人行动，尤指不当行为。

entries.definition: The feeling of being annoyed, or something that causes it.
entries.definitionCN: 恼怒的感觉，或引起恼怒的事物。

normalIntro.en: The word is a call thrown out to someone, and its memories sit on the calling root, on the legal appeal behind it, and on the relatives it gathered along the way.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是朝别人抛出去的一声叫喊，记忆点落在「呼喊」词根、它背后的法律上诉，以及一路收进来的同族词上。

normal.en: Pro- means forward and vocare means to call, so to provoke is literally to call someone out to the front.
normal.cn: pro- 意为向前，vocare 意为呼喊，所以 provoke 字面上就是把人叫到前面来。

normal.en: Provocatio in Roman law was an appeal, so the family has always carried a public, challenging tone.
normal.cn: 罗马法中的 provocatio 是一种上诉，所以这一族词一直带着公开挑战的语气。

normal.en: Provocateur is a French borrowing for a person who stirs trouble on purpose, as in agent provocateur.
normal.cn: provocateur 是来自法语的借词，指故意挑起事端的人，如 agent provocateur。

normal.en: Advocate and provoke share the calling root: one calls someone to your side, the other calls them out.
normal.cn: advocate 与 provoke 共享「呼喊」词根：一个把人叫到你这边，一个把人叫出来对阵。

normal.en: The word is unrelated to provide and province, which come from Latin videre and provincia; only the first syllable looks alike.
normal.cn: 这个词与 provide、province 无关，后两者分别来自拉丁语的 videre 与 provincia；只是开头一个音节看起来相似。

abstract.en: A provocation is a hook thrown out to see what will bite; the word describes the gesture, not the fish.
abstract.cn: 挑衅是抛出的一个钩子，看谁会咬；这个词描述的是动作，不是鱼。

abstract.en: Two people can describe the same act in two directions, one calling it provocation and the other calling it a joke.
abstract.cn: 同一件事，两个人可以从两个方向去称呼：一个叫挑衅，一个叫玩笑。

abstract.en: Law treats provocation as a pressure any ordinary person would feel, which turns a private exchange into a measure of us all.
abstract.cn: 法律把挑衅看成任何常人都承受不住的压力，这就把两个人的争执变成了衡量所有人的尺子。

examples.en: He lashed out at the reporter without any provocation.
examples.cn: 他在没有受到任何挑衅的情况下对那名记者发作。

examples.en: The insult was the provocation that started the whole quarrel.
examples.cn: 那句侮辱就是引起整场争吵的导火索。

examples.en: The defence argued that the killing followed severe provocation.
examples.cn: 辩方主张，那起杀人是在受到严重激惹之后发生的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若佛开申」——听着像「不是佛也开战」，被人一激，凡人也开战，正是挑衅。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ vocare（呼喊）构成 provocare，本义「把人唤出来、挑战」；其名词 provocatio 经古法语 provocation 进入英语。与 provide、provision、province 均不同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a call that dares someone to react; the senses divide into the act of stirring anger, the thing that triggers it, and the pressure the law weighs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一声挑人回应的叫喊」；义项分成激起怒气的行为、触发它的东西，以及法律会权衡的那股压力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone leaning forward and calling another person out, daring them to step over the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人探身向前，高声把另一个人叫出来，挑他越过那条线。

branches.en: a stranger knocking a chair into another table
branches.cn: 陌生人把椅子撞到别人桌上

branches.en: a shouted dare across a crowded room
branches.cn: 拥挤屋子里隔空喊出的挑战

branches.en: a single insult that ends a quiet dinner
branches.cn: 一句侮辱结束了安静的晚餐

branches.en: a barrister describing words that pushed a man past his limit
branches.cn: 律师描述那些把人逼过界限的话

branches.en: the same remark taken as insult here and as excuse there
branches.cn: 同一句话在此处是侮辱、在彼处是理由

intro.en: A Latin prefix of forward movement and a Latin verb of calling hold the word together, and the same stem then grows an adjective, an adverb and a French borrowing.
intro.cn: 表示向前的拉丁语前缀与表示呼喊的拉丁语动词共同支撑这个词，同一词干随后长出形容词、副词和一个法语借词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vocare, to call, the compound provocare, to call forth or challenge, and the noun provocatio are the direct sources of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vocare（呼喊）、复合形式 provocare（唤出、挑战）与名词 provocatio 是英语这个名词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 开处方；开（药）；规定；法令要求；建议采用
definition_en: to order a medicine or treatment for a patient, or to lay down a rule that must be followed
core_image: 医生低头在处方笺上写下一行药名，写完把纸推给病人
scene: 夜里孩子烧得厉害，母亲抱着他冲进急诊室，医生问完症状便低头在纸上写药名。 The doctor prescribed a mild fever medicine and two days of rest.
sceneCN: 这里 prescribe 指「开药、开处方」（第 1 个义项：为病人开出药物或疗法）；句意为医生开了一种温和的退烧药，并让他休息两天。图中可辨识物件：处方笺、笔、急诊室的灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 prescribe 加名词后缀 -tion 构成，义为「处方；药方」，也可指「规定」
由拉丁词干 prescript- 加 -ive 构成，义为「规定性的；规范性的」
由 prescribe 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「开处方的人」

senses.title: To order medicine or treatment for a patient
senses.definition: to write an order for a medicine, treatment, or diet for a sick person
senses.definitionCN: 为病人开出药物、疗法或饮食的书面指示
senses.example: The doctor prescribed a course of antibiotics.
senses.exampleCN: 医生开了一个疗程的抗生素。
senses.why: The Latin verb praescribere meant to write in front, and the slip a doctor hands over still carries that image of words set down before the cure begins.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 praescribere 本义是「写在前面」，医生递过来的那张纸正是先写下的字，药还没吃，指示已经落在纸上，所以「开处方」是这个意象最直接的用法。

senses.title: To lay down a rule that must be obeyed
senses.definition: to state officially what must be done, as a law, rule, or contract does
senses.definitionCN: 以法律、规则或合同的形式正式说明必须做什么
senses.example: The law prescribes a fine for late payment.
senses.exampleCN: 法律规定迟交要罚款。
senses.why: A rule written down before the event works like a doctor's slip: the words come first and the conduct has to follow them.
senses.whyCN: 规则同样是在事情发生之前先写下来，和处方笺一样是「字在前、行为在后」，于是同一个词从医嘱扩展到法律条文。

senses.title: To advise a particular course of action
senses.definition: to recommend strongly that someone do something, especially as a way of improving a situation
senses.definitionCN: 强烈建议某人做某事，尤指为改善某种状况
senses.example: The consultant prescribed a complete change of strategy.
senses.exampleCN: 顾问建议彻底改变策略。
senses.why: Once the word names an expert's written instruction, it can cover any confident recommendation, even when no illness is involved.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词能指专家写下的指示，它就能泛指任何有把握的建议，即使与疾病无关，所以顾问、教练也会「开方子」。

intro.en: Prescribe joins a Latin prefix of place to a Latin verb of writing; the written order came first, and the doctor's slip and the statute both grew out of it.
intro.cn: prescribe 把表示位置的前缀与表示「写」的拉丁动词合在一起；先有写下的指示，处方笺与法律条文都从这一动作长出来。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, marking whatever is placed ahead of something else.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，用来标示被放在某物之前的东西。

items.en: The verb scribere meant to write, and it is generally connected with scratching or cutting marks into a surface.
items.cn: 动词 scribere 意为「写」，一般认为与在表面上刻划痕迹有关。

items.en: Praescribere put the two together: to write at the head of a page, and so to set a rule or direction down in advance.
items.cn: praescribere 把两者合起来：写在页面顶端，引申为预先写下规则或指示。

items.en: Old French prescrire carried both the legal sense of laying something down and the medical sense of ordering a remedy.
items.cn: 古法语 prescrire 同时带有「规定」的法律义与「开药」的医学义。

items.en: English keeps the two branches side by side: a doctor prescribes medicine, and a statute prescribes a penalty.
items.cn: 现代英语把两条分支并列保留：医生开药，法令规定罚则。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for writing; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of ordering and advising.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语「写」的动词展开；近义组收表示命令与建议的动词。

entries.definition: A written order for medicine, or the medicine itself.
entries.definitionCN: 处方；药方，也可指所开的药。

entries.definition: Laying down what should be done or used.
To say what something is like, using words.
entries.definitionCN: 用文字说明某物是什么样子；描述。

entries.definition: To pay regularly to receive a service or publication.
entries.definitionCN: 定期付费订阅服务或刊物。

entries.definition: A text written by hand rather than printed.
To tell someone to do something with authority.
entries.definitionCN: 以权威要求某人做某事；命令。

entries.definition: To state a condition that must be met.
entries.definitionCN: 明确规定必须满足的条件。

entries.definition: To suggest something as a good choice.
To tell someone officially what to do.

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin prefix of place plus a Latin verb for writing, and its family keeps returning to written instructions.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是表示位置的拉丁前缀加表示「写」的拉丁动词，同族词都围绕写下的指示展开。

normal.en: Pre- means before and scribe means write, so prescribe is to write something down before it happens.
normal.cn: pre- 意为「在前」，scribe 意为「写」，所以 prescribe 就是在事情发生前先把话写下来。

normal.en: The same scribe root appears in describe, subscribe and manuscript, all of them about putting words somewhere.
normal.cn: 同一个 scribe 词根也出现在 describe、subscribe、manuscript 里，都跟把字放到某处有关。

normal.en: Prescription is the slip itself, while prescribe is the act of writing it.
normal.cn: prescription 是那张纸本身，prescribe 是写这张纸的动作。

normal.en: A law that prescribes a penalty has already written the punishment into the text.
normal.cn: 一条 prescribes 罚则的法律，早已经把处罚写进了条文里。

normal.en: Prescriptive adds -ive to the stem: an adjective for rules that tell people what to do.
normal.cn: prescriptive 在词干后加 -ive，是形容「规定性规则」的形容词。

abstract.en: The pen moves before the cure does: the order exists on paper first, and the body follows it.
abstract.cn: 笔比疗效先动：指示先落在纸上，身体再照着走。

abstract.en: Every prescription is a small script that the body is asked to follow.
abstract.cn: 每一张处方都是请身体照着演的一小段脚本。

abstract.en: Rules and medicines meet in one word because both are instructions written ahead of time.
abstract.cn: 规则和药物在这个词里相遇，因为两者都是提前写好的指示。

examples.en: The doctor prescribed a mild fever medicine.
examples.cn: 医生开了一种温和的退烧药。

examples.en: The contract prescribes how disputes must be settled.
examples.cn: 合同规定纠纷必须如何解决。

examples.en: She was prescribed two weeks of complete rest.
examples.cn: 医生嘱咐她完全休息两周。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音近「普瑞斯快布」——医生手很快，一张处方像布一样摊开，写满药名。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ scribere（写）构成 praescribere，本义「写在前面」；先写规则、后写药方，于是分化出「规定」与「开处方」两义。

sensesIntro.en: The core act is writing an instruction in advance; the senses divide into medicine, law, and any confident recommendation.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心动作是「预先写下指示」；义项由此分为开药、法律条文与专家的建议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand writing a line of instructions on a slip before anything is carried out.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没开始行动，一只手已在纸上写好一行指示。

branches.en: a slip of paper pushed across the desk
branches.cn: 一张处方笺从桌面推过来

branches.en: a doctor naming both a drug and a way of living
branches.cn: 医生既开药，也嘱咐怎么生活

branches.en: a statute fixing the fine in advance
branches.cn: 法条事先定好罚金

branches.en: a contract and a consultant both telling people what to do
branches.cn: 合同与顾问都在告诉人该怎么做

branches.en: an expert's confident written plan
branches.cn: 专家写下的一份有把握的方案

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin prefix of place, a Latin verb of writing, and the English endings that name the act and its result.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀、表示「写」的拉丁动词，以及命名行为与结果的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to write in front, to lay down
to order medicine or lay down a rule
a written order, especially for medicine
act or result of doing something

latinEntries.meaning: to write in front, to prescribe

definition_zh: 使排成直线；对齐；使一致；校准
definition_en: to place things in a straight line, to make ideas or policies agree, or to adjust a device precisely
core_image: 三枚钉子被打在同一根拉紧的线上，一个也不偏
scene: 工人蹲在地上，眯起一只眼睛，把两块木板推到同一条线上。 He aligned the shelf with the edge of the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 align 是「使对齐、排成直线」（第 1 个义项：把物体摆到同一条线上）；句意为他让架子与墙边对齐。图中可辨识物件：木板、拉线、水平尺。

pos.zh: 动词：使排成直线；对齐；使一致；校准

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「排列；一致；联盟」
由否定前缀加本词构成，义为「使错位、未对齐」
由 misalign 加名词后缀构成，义为「错位；不对齐」

senses.title: To put in a straight line
senses.definition: to place two or more things so that they form a straight line or match up exactly
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多物体摆成一条直线，或使其位置完全对应
senses.example: He aligned the shelf with the edge of the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他让架子与墙边对齐。
senses.why: The French phrase à ligne means 'into line', and the verb still performs exactly that physical act.
senses.whyCN: 法语短语 à ligne 意为「成一条线」，而这个动词至今做的正是这个物理动作。

senses.title: To bring into agreement
senses.definition: to make plans, policies, or interests agree with one another
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、政策或利益彼此吻合
senses.example: The two departments aligned their budgets before the review.
senses.exampleCN: 两个部门在评审前把预算口径统一了。
senses.why: Once things are on one line, they point the same way, so the physical image became a political and managerial one.
senses.whyCN: 物体一旦落在一条线上，就指向同一个方向，于是这个物理画面变成了政治与管理上的说法。

senses.title: To adjust a device precisely
senses.definition: to adjust parts of a machine or instrument so that they work in the correct relative position
senses.definitionCN: 调整机器或仪器的部件，使其处于正确的相对位置
senses.example: The mechanic aligned the front wheels after the repair.
senses.exampleCN: 修好之后，技师做了前轮定位。
senses.why: Machines need their parts on the same axis, so the general idea of lining up became a technical procedure with a name.
senses.whyCN: 机器需要各部件处在同一轴线上，于是「排成线」这个一般观念变成了一道有名字的技术工序。

intro.en: Align is a French phrase pulled into English as a verb: à ligne, 'into line'.
intro.cn: align 是一个被英语吸收为动词的法语短语：à ligne，意为「成一条线」。

items.en: Linea meant 'a line, a string', and it is the source of line and of align.
items.cn: linea 意为「线、绳」，是 line 与 align 的共同来源。

items.en: The phrase à ligne, 'into line', described soldiers or objects set in a row.
items.cn: 短语 à ligne「成一条线」用于描述排成一列的士兵或物件。

items.en: French made the verb aligner from the phrase, meaning 'to put into line'.
items.cn: 法语由这个短语造出动词 aligner，意为「摆成一条线」。

items.en: English borrowed aligner as align, first in military and surveying contexts.
items.cn: 英语借入作 align，最初用于军事与测量场合。

items.en: The figurative sense of aligning policies or interests is a twentieth-century extension.
items.cn: 「使政策或利益一致」的比喻义是二十世纪的扩展。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on align; the near-meaning group gathers ways of matching things up.
note.cn: 形近组收由 align 构成的词；近义组收使事物彼此对应的说法。

entries.definition: The state of being in line, or an alliance of interests.
entries.definitionCN: 成一条线的状态，或利益上的结盟。

entries.definition: To put out of line or out of agreement.
A state of being wrongly positioned.
To arrange people or things in a row.
To make different activities work together smoothly.
To change something slightly so that it works or fits better.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微改变某物使其更合适或更好用。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the Latin noun linea and the French phrase à ligne.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：拉丁名词 linea 与法语短语 à ligne。

normal.en: Align is 'a line' turned into a verb: to put things a-line.
normal.cn: align 就是把「一条线」变成动词：把东西摆成一条线。

normal.en: The same word works on shelves, budgets and wheels, because all three need to sit on one axis.
normal.cn: 同一个词能用于架子、预算与车轮，因为三者都需要落在同一轴线上。

normal.en: Alignment is the noun; misalignment adds the idea of going wrong.
normal.cn: alignment 是名词；misalignment 加上了「出了偏差」的意思。

normal.en: Non-aligned countries stay outside a bloc, literally off the line.
normal.cn: non-aligned 国家置身集团之外，字面上就是「不在那条线上」。

normal.en: One l, then i: a-l-i-g-n, and the g is silent.
normal.cn: 一个 l 后接 i：a-l-i-g-n，其中 g 不发音。

abstract.en: Alignment is a physical idea that becomes a moral one: people who agree are said to be on the same line.
abstract.cn: 对齐本是物理观念，后来成了道德观念：意见相同的人被说成在同一条线上。

abstract.en: To align interests is to admit that they were not aligned before.
abstract.cn: 说「使利益一致」，就等于承认此前并不一致。

abstract.en: A machine out of alignment still runs, which is why small misalignments are the hardest to notice.
abstract.cn: 失准的机器照样能转，所以轻微的错位最难被察觉。

examples.en: He aligned the shelf with the edge of the wall.
examples.cn: 他让架子与墙边对齐。

examples.en: The two departments aligned their budgets before the review.
examples.cn: 两个部门在评审前把预算口径统一了。

examples.en: The mechanic aligned the front wheels after the repair.
examples.cn: 修好之后，技师做了前轮定位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额，来嗯」——额，来，嗯，把桌角都摆到一条线上。

root: 源自法语短语 à ligne「成一条线」及其动词 aligner，词根为拉丁语 linea「线」。

sensesIntro.en: One line runs through all three senses: objects on it, plans on it, and machine parts on it.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项贯穿着同一条线：物体落在线上、计划落在线上、机器部件也落在线上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three nails driven along a taut string, none of them off by a hair.
core.cn: 核心意象：三枚钉子沿一根拉紧的线钉下，一枚也不偏。

branches.en: a shelf pushed level with a wall edge
branches.cn: 被推到与墙边齐平的架子

branches.en: two budgets rewritten to the same assumptions
branches.cn: 按同一套假设重写的两份预算

branches.en: front wheels set on a measuring rig
branches.cn: 在测量架上校准的前轮

branches.en: a party agreeing to a coalition platform
branches.cn: 同意同一份联合纲领的政党

branches.en: one straight line, drawn by hand and by instrument
branches.cn: 同一条直线，用手画，也用仪器校

intro.en: A Latin noun for a line, the French phrase built on it, and the English endings that extend it.
intro.cn: 一个意为「线」的拉丁名词、建在其上的法语短语，以及扩展它的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: linea is recorded Latin; the verb itself was formed in French.
latinIntro.cn: linea 是有文献记录的拉丁词，动词本身则是在法语中构成的。

items.meaning: the state of being in line

definition_zh: 外国的；陌生的；格格不入的；外国人；外星人
definition_en: belonging to another country, strange and unfamiliar, or a person from another country or planet
core_image: 一个人站在热闹的街口，四周的话他一句也听不懂
scene: 夜市里人声鼎沸，他站在摊子前，听不懂旁边的人在说什么。 The customs officer asked whether he was an alien or a resident.
sceneCN: 这里 alien 是「外国人、外侨」（第 4 个义项：法律意义上不属本国的人）；句意为海关人员问他是外侨还是居民。图中可辨识物件：夜市摊子、行李箱、证件。

pos.zh: 形容词：外国的；陌生的；格格不入的
名词：外国人；外侨；外星人

derivatives.zh: 由本词加动词后缀构成，义为「使疏远；使格格不入」
由 alienate 加名词后缀构成，义为「疏离；异化」
由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「陌生感；异质性」

senses.title: Belonging to another country
senses.definition: belonging to or coming from a country that is not one's own
senses.definitionCN: 属于或来自非本国的国家
senses.example: The plant is an alien species that spread along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物是沿河扩散的外来物种。
senses.why: Latin alienus meant 'belonging to another', so the word marks anything that belongs to someone else's place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alienus 意为「属于他人的」，所以这个词标记的是归属于别人那处地方的东西。

senses.title: Strange and unwelcome
senses.definition: strange, unfamiliar, and therefore difficult to accept or fit into
senses.definitionCN: 陌生、不熟悉，因此难以接受或融入
senses.example: The rules felt alien to everything she had been taught.
senses.exampleCN: 这些规则与她所受的一切教导都格格不入。
senses.why: What belongs elsewhere can also feel wrong here, so the word shifted from ownership to emotional distance.
senses.whyCN: 属于别处的东西，在这里也可能让人觉得不对劲，于是这个词从「归属」转向了情感上的距离。

senses.title: A being from another planet
senses.definition: in science fiction, a creature from another planet
senses.definitionCN: 科幻作品里来自其他星球的生物
senses.example: The film shows an alien learning to speak through music.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片讲一个外星人通过音乐学会说话。
senses.why: Twentieth-century science fiction reused the legal word for a foreigner and moved the border from a country to a planet.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪科幻沿用了这个法律词，把边界从国界搬到了星球之间。

senses.title: A foreign national, in law
senses.definition: in law, a person who is not a citizen of the country in which they are
senses.definitionCN: 法律上不属所在国公民的人
senses.example: The customs officer asked whether he was an alien or a resident.
senses.exampleCN: 海关人员问他是外侨还是居民。
senses.why: Legal writing needed a neutral term for non-citizens, and the old adjective supplied it; the usage is now often replaced by foreign national.
senses.whyCN: 法律文书需要一个中性词指非公民，这个古老形容词正好补位；如今这一用法多被 foreign national 取代。

intro.en: Alien goes back to a Latin word for 'belonging to another', and every sense still turns on that idea of elsewhere.
intro.cn: alien 可追到拉丁语中意为「属于他人」的词，所有义项都围绕「属于别处」这个念头。

items.en: Alius meant 'other', the root of alias, alter and alien alike.
items.cn: alius 意为「其他的」，alias、alter 与 alien 都出自这个词。

items.en: Alienus meant 'belonging to another, foreign', and could describe both persons and things.
items.cn: alienus 意为「属于他人的、外来的」，既可形容人也可形容物。

items.en: French carried the word into law and diplomacy, where it named a person outside the community.
items.cn: 法语把这个词带入法律与外交，用来指群体之外的人。

items.en: English uses alien from the fourteenth century for foreigners and for things that do not belong.
items.cn: 英语自十四世纪起用 alien 指外国人，也指不属于本地的事物。

items.en: Science fiction added the planetary sense in the twentieth century, and the legal sense has since softened.
items.cn: 科幻在二十世纪加入「外星」义，法律义此后逐渐软化。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same 'other' root; the near-meaning group gathers outsiders and unfamiliar things.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「其他」词根的词；近义组收外来者与陌生事物。

entries.definition: To make someone feel unwelcome or distant.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人感到不受欢迎或疏远。

entries.definition: The feeling of being cut off from a group or from oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 与群体或与自我割裂的感觉。

entries.definition: A false name used by a person.
Belonging to a country other than one's own.
A person one does not know.
Unfamiliar in a way that is interesting rather than threatening.
entries.definitionCN: 陌生但有趣，而非令人不安的。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: Latin alius, 'other', and the adjective ending -enus.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：拉丁语 alius「其他的」与形容词词尾 -enus。

normal.en: Alien, alias and alter all begin with the same idea: the other one.
normal.cn: alien、alias、alter 都从同一个念头开始：另一个。

normal.en: Alien to means foreign to, and it is the phrase that carries the emotional sense.
normal.cn: alien to 意为「与……格格不入」，情绪义就藏在这个搭配里。

normal.en: The legal noun is neutral, the science-fiction noun is exciting: context does the work.
normal.cn: 法律名词是中性的，科幻名词是刺激的：意义由语境完成。

normal.en: The stress is on the first syllable: A-li-en.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：A-li-en。

normal.en: Keep the i before the e: a-l-i-e-n.
normal.cn: 注意 i 在 e 前：a-l-i-e-n。

abstract.en: A word for 'belonging to another' can describe a plant, a law, a feeling and a planet, because otherness takes many forms.
abstract.cn: 一个「属于他人」的词既能形容植物、法律、感受，也能形容星球，因为「他者」有许多形态。

abstract.en: The same word that excludes can also fascinate, which is why alien and exotic sit so close together.
abstract.cn: 同一个用于排斥的词也能令人着迷，所以 alien 与 exotic 靠得那么近。

abstract.en: Calling someone an alien is always a statement about the border, not about the person.
abstract.cn: 把某人称作 alien，说的永远是边界，而不是那个人。

examples.en: The customs officer asked whether he was an alien or a resident.
examples.cn: 海关人员问他是外侨还是居民。

examples.en: The rules felt alien to everything she had been taught.
examples.cn: 这些规则与她所受的一切教导都格格不入。

examples.en: The film shows an alien learning to speak through music.
examples.cn: 这部影片讲一个外星人通过音乐学会说话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱连」——爱连家乡都不认识他，他成了这里的外人。

root: 源自拉丁语 alienus「属于他人的、外来的」，其词根 alius 意为「其他的」。

sensesIntro.en: One idea of elsewhere runs through all four senses: another country, another culture, another planet, and the legal line drawn around a community.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项贯穿着同一个「别处」：别的国家、别的文化、别的星球，以及围绕共同体划下的那条法律界线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller stands at a busy corner and understands not one word around him.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个旅人站在热闹的街口，周围的话一句也听不懂。

branches.en: a plant that spreads where it was never native
branches.cn: 在并非原生之地蔓延的植物

branches.en: a rule book written in a language of its own
branches.cn: 用另一套语言写成的规则手册

branches.en: a light crossing the sky too fast to be a plane
branches.cn: 快得不像飞机的天上光点

branches.en: a form with two boxes: citizen and other
branches.cn: 只有「公民」与「其他」两栏的表格

branches.en: one outside position, felt and also filed
branches.cn: 同一个「在外」的位置，既被感受，也被归档

intro.en: A Latin root for 'other', its adjective, and the English endings that build the family.
intro.cn: 一个意为「其他」的拉丁词根、它的形容词形式，以及构成词族的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: alius and alienus are recorded Latin; the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: alius 与 alienus 都是有文献记录的拉丁词，更早的印欧词根属重构。

definition_zh: 表面的；肤浅的
definition_en: only on the surface, not deep or thorough
core_image: 只擦掉桌面上的灰，却没有看见桌下的裂痕
scene: 他的伤只是表面的，并不严重。 His injury was only superficial and not serious.
sceneCN: 这里 superficial 是「表面的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的伤只是表面的，并不严重。

senses.title: On the surface only
senses.definition: existing only on the outer layer
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于外层
senses.example: His injury was only superficial and not serious.
senses.exampleCN: 他的伤只是表面的，并不严重。
senses.why: This is the physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理层面的义项。

senses.title: Not deep or thorough
senses.definition: not going deeply into a subject
senses.definitionCN: 没有深入探讨某一主题
senses.example: The report gives only a superficial analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告只做了肤浅的分析。
senses.why: Here the word criticizes shallow thinking.
senses.whyCN: 这里批评的是思考浅薄。

intro.en: Superficial comes from Latin superficies, the surface.
intro.cn: superficial 来自拉丁语 superficies，意为表面。

items.en: Super meant above.
items.cn: super 意为在上。

items.en: Facies meant face or form.
items.cn: facies 意为脸、外形。

items.en: Superficies meant the surface.
items.cn: superficies 意为表面。

items.en: Superficialis meant of the surface.
items.cn: superficialis 意为表面的。

items.en: Superficial also meant shallow.
items.cn: superficial 也指肤浅的。

note.en: Superficial is compared with look-alike words and with words for shallowness.
note.cn: 把 superficial 与形近词以及表示浅薄的词作比较。

the state of being shallow
better than another
not deep

normalIntro.en: Superficial means staying on the surface and never going under it.
normalIntro.cn: superficial 就是停在表面，从不潜入下面。

normal.en: His injury was only superficial and not serious.
normal.cn: 他的伤只是表面的，并不严重。

normal.en: The report gives only a superficial analysis.
normal.cn: 这份报告只做了肤浅的分析。

normal.en: There is a superficial resemblance between the two.
normal.cn: 两者之间只有表面的相似。

normal.en: Superficial damage is easy to repair.
normal.cn: 表面损伤容易修复。

normal.en: His knowledge of the subject is superficial.
normal.cn: 他对这个主题的了解很肤浅。

abstract.en: Superficial is a glance pretending to be a look.
abstract.cn: 肤浅，是一瞥假装成凝视。

abstract.en: The surface is true, but it is not the whole truth.
abstract.cn: 表面是真的，但不是全部真相。

abstract.en: Depth begins where the surface stops being enough.
abstract.cn: 当表面不再够用，深度就开始了。

examples.en: Superficial damage is easy to repair.
examples.cn: 表面损伤容易修复。

dict_mnemonic.text: superficial 由拉丁语「在上」与「面」组成，表示只在表面的；引申为知识或分析肤浅的。

root: 来自拉丁语 superficies（表面），由 super（在上）与 facies（面）组成，字面是「最上面的一层」。

sensesIntro.en: Superficial means only on the outer layer, or not deep in thought.
sensesIntro.cn: superficial 表示只在外层，也可指思考或知识不深入。

core.en: Only the top layer of a thing.
core.cn: 事物最上面的那一层。

branches.en: His injury was only superficial and not serious.
branches.cn: 他的伤只是表面的，并不严重。

intro.en: Superficial builds superficially and superficiality.
intro.cn: superficial 可构成 superficially 和 superficiality。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin facies, face, with super above.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语 facies（面），加上 super（在上）。

items.example: The critic noted the superficiality of the film.
items.exampleCN: 评论家指出这部电影的肤浅。

items.example: The superficialness of the plan worried them.
items.exampleCN: 计划的表面性让他们担心。

definition_zh: 陷阱；圈套；捕捉；困住；使陷入困境
definition_en: a device or plan for catching something, or to catch and hold something so it cannot escape
core_image: 草丛里一块铺了落叶的木板，脚一踩便弹起铁夹
scene: 林子里，猎人在兽径上安了一块带机关的木板，上面盖了层落叶。 A rabbit was caught in the trap before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 trap 是「陷阱」（第 1 个义项：捕捉用的装置）；句意为天亮前一只兔子落进了陷阱。盖着落叶的木板与铁夹正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -er 构成，义为「设陷阱捕兽的人」
现在分词名词化，义为「捕捉；捕兽业」；复数指马饰
加前缀 en- 构成，义为「诱捕；使陷入」

senses.title: A device for catching animals
senses.definition: a device, often hidden, that catches and holds an animal
senses.definitionCN: 常被藏起来的装置，用来抓住并留住动物
senses.example: The farmer set traps for the rats.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫设了捕鼠夹。
senses.why: The word is an old English name for a snare, and its whole sense is a hidden catch that closes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是古英语里对罗网的称呼，全部含义就是一道藏起来的、会合上的机关。

senses.title: A plan that deceives someone
senses.definition: a trick or plan that makes someone do what you want
senses.definitionCN: 诱使别人按你的意图行动的计谋
senses.example: The offer was a trap to get his signature.
senses.exampleCN: 那个提议是个骗他签字的圈套。
senses.why: A snare for an animal and a snare for a person share the same shape: a hidden catch.
senses.whyCN: 给动物设的套与给人的套形状相同：都是藏起来的机关。

senses.title: A bad situation one cannot leave
senses.definition: a difficult situation that is hard to escape from
senses.definitionCN: 难以脱身的艰难处境
senses.example: Debt can become a trap for young families.
senses.exampleCN: 债务可能成为年轻家庭的困境。
senses.why: When the catch is circumstances rather than jaws, the word still pictures something closing around a person.
senses.whyCN: 当合上的不是铁夹而是处境，这个词画的仍是有什么在人周围合拢。

senses.title: To catch and hold an animal
senses.definition: to catch an animal in a trap or by a similar means
senses.definitionCN: 用陷阱或类似办法抓住动物
senses.example: They trapped rabbits in the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在果园里捕兔。
senses.why: The verb is the action the noun describes: to close the catch on something.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词描述的那个动作：把机关合在某个东西上。

senses.title: To prevent from escaping
senses.definition: to hold people or things somewhere so they cannot move or leave
senses.definitionCN: 把人或物留在某处，使其动不了或走不了
senses.example: Rescuers freed the miners trapped underground.
senses.exampleCN: 救援人员救出了困在地下的矿工。
senses.why: Prisons and collapses both close a space around a person, which is the trap image without the jaws.
senses.whyCN: 监牢与塌方都在人身周围合拢一块空间，这正是去掉铁夹的陷阱画面。

senses.title: To hold heat or gas in place
senses.definition: to keep heat, gas, or light from escaping
senses.definitionCN: 不让热、气或光跑掉
senses.example: Thick walls trap warmth in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 厚墙在冬天能留住热量。
senses.why: A layer that does not let something out acts like a trap that does not let something in.
senses.whyCN: 一层不让东西出去的材料，就像一道不让东西进来的陷阱。

intro.en: The noun is an old English word for a snare, and the verb grows from it in the same period.
intro.cn: 这是古英语里表示罗网的名词，动词也在同一时期由它生出。

items.en: Treppe means a snare or trap, and is used of devices for catching wild animals.
items.cn: 古英语 treppe 意为罗网、陷阱，指捕捉野兽的装置。

items.en: The word has relatives in Dutch and Low German, all naming a catching device.
items.cn: 这个词在荷兰语与低地德语里都有亲族，都指捕捉装置。

items.en: The noun widens from animal snares to tricks that catch people.
items.cn: 中世纪英语里，这个名词从兽夹扩展到能套住人的计谋。

items.en: Railways and mining give the verb its sense of being shut in and unable to escape.
items.cn: 铁路与采矿给了动词「被困住、逃不掉」的义项。

items.en: Modern technology adds the sense of holding heat, gas, or light where it is wanted.
items.cn: 现代技术又添上「把热、气或光留在该留之处」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words that differ by one letter, while the near-meaning group names other snares and holds.
note.cn: 形近组汇集只差一个字母的短词，近义组列出其他圈套与困住的说法。

normalIntro.en: Four letters, but the image does all the work.
normalIntro.cn: 只有四个字母，但画面就能记住。

normal.en: Think of a trap door: the same short word sits in front.
normal.cn: 想想 trap door（活板门）：同一个短词就在前面。

normal.en: A trapper is the person, trapping is the work.
normal.cn: trapper 是人，trapping 是那份活。

normal.en: Entrap adds en- to make a verb of catching someone in a trick.

normal.en: A speed trap catches cars, not rabbits, with the same logic.
normal.cn: 测速陷阱抓的是车不是兔，逻辑却一样。

abstract.en: Picture leaves over a board, and the board springs up.
abstract.cn: 想象落叶盖着木板，木板一下弹起。

abstract.en: Hear the click before you see the jaws.
abstract.cn: 先听见那咔哒声，再看见铁夹。

abstract.en: Feel a space close around you, walls instead of jaws.
abstract.cn: 再感受空间在你周围合上，墙代替了铁夹。

examples.en: The mouse escaped the trap twice.
examples.cn: 那只老鼠两次逃出了捕鼠夹。

examples.en: They were trapped in the elevator for an hour.
examples.cn: 他们被困在电梯里一个小时。

examples.en: The glass traps heat from the winter sun.
examples.cn: 这种玻璃能留住冬日阳光的热量。

root: 古英语 treppe（罗网、捕兽器），与荷兰语、低地德语同源；同族有 trapper、trapping、entrap

sensesIntro.en: The word always pictures something closing around a thing so that it cannot get out.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词总是画着「有什么在某物周围合上，让它出不来」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board hidden under leaves, snapping shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：盖在落叶下的木板，一下合上。

branches.en: The physical pair: the device and the act of catching with it.
branches.cn: 实物一对：装置，以及用装置去抓的动作。

branches.en: The trick sense, where the snare is a plan aimed at a person.
branches.cn: 诡计义：罗网是针对人设的计划。

branches.en: The confinement senses, where circumstances take the place of jaws.
branches.cn: 困住义：处境取代了铁夹。

branches.en: The physical containment sense, where heat is what cannot get out.
branches.cn: 物理封存义：出不去的是热。

branches.en: The catching sense, where a hunter closes the jaws on a rabbit.
branches.cn: 捕捉义：猎人在兔子身上合上铁夹。

intro.en: This is a native word, so the pieces are suffixes rather than Latin roots.
intro.cn: 这是本族词，所以拆出来的是后缀而非拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The stem trapp- appears in trapper, trapping, and the verb entrap.
latinIntro.cn: 词干 trapp- 出现在 trapper、trapping 与动词 entrap 里。

items.example: The stem is the whole of trap.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干就是 trap 的全部。
en- 加 trap 成为 entrap。

items.example: They tried to entrap the witness.
items.exampleCN: 他们试图诱使证人落套。

items.example: The climbers were trapped by snow.
Trapping was once common in the north.
items.exampleCN: 捕兽业曾在北方很常见。

items.meaning: loops of wire for catching birds
items.example: Old snares were loops, not jaws.
items.exampleCN: old snares 指套索，不是铁夹。

definition_zh: 达到；获得
definition_en: to reach a goal or level after effort, or to gain something
core_image: 手终于够到高处的横杆
scene: 她练了三年才拿到那张证书。 After years of study she attained her goal.
sceneCN: 这里 attain 是「达到」（第 1 个义项：经过努力抵达目标）；句意是多年学习后她达到了目标。

senses.title: Reach a goal
senses.definition: to reach a goal, level or age after effort
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力抵达某个目标、水平或年龄
senses.example: After years of study she attained her goal.
senses.exampleCN: 多年学习之后她达到了目标。
senses.why: Attain comes from Latin attingere, 'to touch', from ad- 'to' and tangere 'to touch', so success is pictured as a hand finally reaching the bar.
senses.whyCN: attain 源自拉丁语 attingere「触到」，由 ad-「向」与 tangere「触」构成，成功被画成一只手终于够到横杆。

senses.title: Gain or acquire
senses.definition: to gain something such as a reputation or a position
senses.definitionCN: 取得名声、地位等抽象之物
senses.example: He attained a reputation for honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 他获得了诚实的名声。
senses.why: What a hand can touch includes not only a height but also honour and rank, so the reaching verb comes to mean acquiring.
senses.whyCN: 手能够到的不只是高度，还有荣誉与地位，于是这个「够到」的动词就有了「获得」的含义。

intro.en: Attain is a Latin word of touching, and achievement is pictured as reaching something.
intro.cn: attain 是拉丁语中表示「触碰」的词，成就被画成够到某物。

items.en: tangere meant 'to touch'.
items.cn: tangere 意为「触碰」。

items.en: attingere meant 'to touch or reach'.
items.cn: attingere 意为「触到、够到」。

items.en: ateindre meant 'to reach a goal'.
items.cn: ateindre 意为「抵达目标」。

items.en: English attain covered reaching and gaining.
items.cn: 英语 attain 兼指达到与获得。

items.en: The word now sounds formal and is common in writing.
items.cn: 这个词如今偏正式，常见于书面语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tain stem; the near-meaning group gives verbs of reaching and winning.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tain 词干；近义组是表示抵达与取得的动词。

normalIntro.en: To attain is to get your hand on the bar at last.
normalIntro.cn: attain 就是手终于搭上那根横杆。

normal.en: It is formal; in speech people usually say reach or achieve.
normal.cn: 它偏正式，口语里更常说 reach 或 achieve。

normal.en: The object is often abstract: a goal, a level, a standard.
normal.cn: 宾语常是抽象名词：目标、水平、标准。

normal.en: The noun is attainment, not attain.
normal.cn: 名词是 attainment。

normal.en: The tain part also appears in contain and retain.
normal.cn: tain 这一部分也出现在 contain 与 retain 中。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: at-TAIN.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See fingers closing around a high bar.
abstract.cn: 想象手指终于扣住高处横杆。

abstract.en: See a certificate handed over after long practice.
abstract.cn: 想象长期练习后递来的一纸证书。

abstract.en: See a line on a chart finally touched.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上的那条线终于被碰到。

examples.en: After years of study she attained her goal.
examples.cn: 多年学习之后她达到了目标。

examples.en: He attained a reputation for honesty.
examples.cn: 他获得了诚实的名声。

examples.en: The team attained the highest standard in the test.
examples.cn: 这支队伍在测试中达到了最高标准。

dict_mnemonic.text: at-（向）加 tain（触）：手向高处伸去，终于触到，就是达到；够到名声与地位，就是获得。

root: 源自拉丁语 attingere「触到」，由 ad-「向」与 tangere「触」构成，经古法语 ateindre 进入英语；由「够到」具体高度引申为达到目标与获得名声。

sensesIntro.en: Height and honour are both things a reaching hand can close on.
sensesIntro.cn: 高度与荣誉，都是伸出的手能够握住的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fingers touching the bar.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖碰到横杆。

branches.cn: 达到目标

branches.cn: 达到标准

branches.en: attain maturity
branches.cn: 达到成熟

branches.en: attain a reputation
branches.cn: 获得名声

branches.cn: 取得职位

intro.en: The tain root, 'to hold or touch', also shapes contain, retain and maintain.
intro.cn: 词根 tain 意为「握住、触及」，也构成 contain、retain 与 maintain。

latinIntro.en: Latin tangere, 'to touch', is the source; its participle tactus gives tact and contact.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tangere「触」是来源，其分词 tactus 产生了 tact 与 contact。

definition_zh: 海湾；巨大差距；深渊
definition_en: a large area of sea partly surrounded by land, or a great difference between people
core_image: 海岸线向内凹进一大片平静的海水
scene: 小船驶入平静的海湾。 The boat entered the calm gulf.
sceneCN: 这里 gulf 是「海湾」（第 1 个义项）；句意：小船驶入平静的海湾。

senses.title: Sea inlet
senses.definition: a large area of sea partly surrounded by land
senses.definitionCN: 部分被陆地包围的大片海域
senses.example: The boat entered the calm gulf.
senses.exampleCN: 小船驶入平静的海湾。
senses.why: This is the geographic sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是地理义项。

senses.title: Great difference
senses.definition: a large separation between people or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 人或观念之间的巨大隔阂
senses.example: A gulf opened between the two sides.
senses.exampleCN: 双方之间出现了一道鸿沟。
senses.why: The wide water became a metaphor for distance.
senses.whyCN: 宽阔的水面成了距离的隐喻。

senses.title: Deep opening
senses.definition: a deep hollow or whirlpool
senses.definitionCN: 深陷的空洞或漩涡
senses.example: The ship sank into the gulf.
senses.exampleCN: 船沉入了深渊。
senses.why: An older sense stressed depth and swallowing.
senses.whyCN: 较古老的义项强调深度与吞噬。

intro.en: Gulf comes from French golfe, from Latin colphus, from Greek kolpos, a bosom or bay.
intro.cn: gulf 来自法语 golfe，经拉丁语 colphus 上溯至希腊语 kolpos（胸怀、海湾）。

items.en: Kolpos meant a bosom or a bay.
items.cn: kolpos 意为胸怀或海湾。

items.en: Colphus named a bay.
items.cn: colphus 指海湾。

items.en: Golfe meant a large bay.
items.cn: golfe 意为大海湾。

items.en: Gulf named a deep inlet of the sea.
items.cn: gulf 指海中深深凹入的水域。

items.en: The word became a metaphor for separation.
items.cn: 这个词成为「隔阂」的隐喻。

note.en: Gulf is compared with look-alike words and words for bays or gaps.
note.cn: 把 gulf 与形近词以及表示海湾或差距的词作比较。

entries.definition: a game played with a small ball
a seabird with long wings
to swallow quickly
a curved part of the coast
an empty space between things
a very deep hole

normalIntro.en: Gulf is water curved into land, and then any wide distance between people.
normalIntro.cn: gulf 是凹进陆地的海水，后来也指人与人之间的宽阔距离。

normal.en: Warm water flows through the gulf.
normal.cn: 温暖的海水流过海湾。

normal.en: The gulf between them widened.
normal.cn: 他们之间的鸿沟加深了。

normal.en: They tried to bridge the gulf.
normal.cn: 他们试图弥合鸿沟。

normal.en: The Persian Gulf is busy.
normal.cn: 波斯湾十分繁忙。

normal.en: The storm rose over the gulf.
normal.cn: 风暴在海湾上空升起。

abstract.en: Water between two shores keeps them apart.
abstract.cn: 两片海岸之间的水，把它们隔开。

abstract.en: A word can be a bridge or a gulf.
abstract.cn: 一句话，可以是桥，也可以是鸿沟。

abstract.en: Distance is measured in more than miles.
abstract.cn: 距离，不只以里数衡量。

examples.cn: 小船驶入平静的海湾。

examples.en: A gulf opened between the two sides.
examples.cn: 双方之间出现了一道鸿沟。

examples.en: The ship sank into the gulf.
examples.cn: 船沉入了深渊。

dict_mnemonic.text: gulf 是「海湾」，也指「巨大差距、鸿沟」；the Gulf 常指波斯湾地区，bridge the gulf 是弥合鸿沟；复数加 s 变 gulfs。

root: 来自法语 golfe，经拉丁语 colphus 上溯至希腊语 kolpos（胸怀、海湾）；由凹入陆地的海面引申为人际与观念之间的巨大隔阂。

sensesIntro.en: Gulf means a sea inlet, a great difference, or a deep opening.
sensesIntro.cn: gulf 指海湾、巨大差距，或深渊。

core.en: A wide curve of sea cutting into land.
core.cn: 切入陆地的宽阔海面。

branches.en: Warm water curves between two coasts.
branches.cn: 温暖的海水在两片海岸间弯入。

branches.en: Two people sit far apart at a table.
branches.cn: 两人在桌边坐得很远。

branches.en: Dark water opens beneath a hull.
branches.cn: 船身下裂开深暗的水面。

branches.en: The wide water becomes a wide silence.
branches.cn: 宽阔的水面，变成宽阔的沉默。

branches.en: A bay can also be deep and dangerous.
branches.cn: 海湾也可能又深又险。

intro.en: Gulf forms plurals and a few place compounds.
intro.cn: gulf 构成复数和若干地名复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is colphus, from Greek kolpos.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁语源头是 colphus，来自希腊语 kolpos。

items.example: Warm gulfs lie to the south.

items.example: The Gulf Stream warms the coast.
items.exampleCN: 墨西哥湾流使海岸变暖。

a war in the Gulf region

items.exampleCN: 这个海湾国家出口石油。

definition_zh: 铝；铝材
definition_en: a light silvery metal that does not rust easily, used for cans, foil, and aircraft parts
core_image: 一卷银亮的铝箔在厨房台面上展开
scene: 厨房里，她把剩菜用铝箔包好，放进冰箱。 She wrapped the leftovers in aluminium foil.
sceneCN: 这里 aluminium 是「铝」（第 1 个义项：一种轻而耐锈的银白色金属）；句意是她用铝箔把剩菜包好。

senses.title: The metal element
senses.definition: the chemical element of atomic number thirteen, a light silvery metal that resists corrosion
senses.definitionCN: 原子序数为十三的化学元素，是轻质银白色且耐腐蚀的金属
senses.example: Aluminium is extracted from bauxite by electrolysis.
senses.exampleCN: 铝通过电解从铝土矿中提炼出来。
senses.why: The name comes from Latin alumen, 'alum', the mineral from which the metal was first isolated, so the word begins as a chemical label.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自拉丁语 alumen「明矾」，即最早分离出该金属的矿物，所以这个词起初是化学名称。

senses.title: The metal as a material
senses.definition: the metal considered as an everyday manufacturing material, as in foil, cans, and frames
senses.definitionCN: 把这种金属当作日常制造材料来用，如铝箔、铝罐与框架
senses.example: The window frames are made of aluminium, not steel.
senses.exampleCN: 窗框是铝制的，不是钢的。
senses.why: Because the metal is light and does not rust, industry talks about aluminium as a material to be shaped, which is why it appears in foil, cans, and aircraft.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种金属轻且不生锈，工业界把它当作可加工的材料来谈，因此它出现在铝箔、铝罐与飞机部件中。

intro.en: Aluminium is a modern scientific name built on the Latin word for alum.
intro.cn: aluminium 是建立在拉丁语「明矾」一词上的现代科学名称。

items.en: alumen meant 'alum', the mineral salt used in dyeing and medicine.
items.cn: alumen 意为「明矾」，是用于染色与医药的矿物盐。

items.en: English kept alum for the mineral, the source of the metal's name.
items.cn: 英语以 alum 保留了这个矿物名，它正是金属名称的来源。

items.en: Humphry Davy proposed aluminum for the newly isolated metal.
items.cn: 汉弗莱·戴维在 1808 年为新分离出的金属提出 aluminum 这一名称。

items.en: Writers adopted aluminium to match other elements ending in -ium.
items.cn: 人们采用 aluminium，以与其他以 -ium 结尾的元素名一致。

items.en: American English kept Davy's aluminum, while British English kept aluminium.
items.cn: 美式英语沿用戴维的 aluminum，英式英语则用 aluminium。

note.en: The look-alike group covers the spellings and the ore; the near-meaning group places it among metals.
note.cn: 形近组涵盖拼写与矿石；近义组把它放进金属类别。

entries.definition: the American name for the same metal
a mineral salt used in dyeing
aluminium oxide, the white powder from which the metal is refined
entries.definitionCN: 氧化铝，提炼金属用的白色粉末

entries.definition: a hard shiny material that conducts heat and electricity
entries.definitionCN: 坚硬有光泽、能导热导电的材料

entries.definition: a metal mixed with another element
entries.definitionCN: 与其他元素混合的金属

entries.definition: the ore from which aluminium is extracted

normalIntro.en: Aluminium carries the Latin word for alum inside it.
normalIntro.cn: aluminium 里藏着拉丁语的「明矾」一词。

normal.en: Alum plus -inium: the metal from alum.
normal.cn: alum 加 -inium：从明矾来的金属。

normal.en: British aluminium, American aluminum.
normal.cn: 英式写 aluminium，美式写 aluminum。

normal.en: Aluminium foil is the everyday meeting point.
normal.cn: 铝箔是这个词最常见的日常场景。

normal.en: It is light, so it flies: aircraft use aluminium alloys.
normal.cn: 它很轻，所以能飞：飞机构件用铝合金。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: al-u-MIN-i-um.
normal.cn: 重音在第三个音节：al-u-MIN-i-um。

abstract.en: Picture a roll of silver foil unrolling.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷银色铝箔展开。

abstract.en: See a row of drink cans on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象货架上一排饮料罐。

abstract.en: Imagine a light bicycle frame lifted with one hand.
abstract.cn: 想象单手提起的轻质车架。

examples.en: Aluminium is lighter than steel and does not rust.
examples.cn: 铝比钢轻，而且不会生锈。

examples.en: She covered the tray with aluminium foil before baking.
examples.cn: 烘烤前她用铝箔盖住了烤盘。

examples.en: The factory recycles aluminium cans collected from the city.
examples.cn: 这家工厂回收从城里收集来的铝罐。

dict_mnemonic.text: alum（明矾）加 -inium：从明矾里炼出的银白金属，就是铝。

root: 源自拉丁语 alumen「明矾」，英语作 alum；1808 年戴维为新分离的金属造出 aluminum，1812 年又出现 aluminium，以与多数以 -ium 结尾的元素名统一，形成英美两种拼写并存的局面。

sensesIntro.en: The same metal is named twice over: as a chemical element and as a material of industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种金属有两个侧面：化学元素与工业材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a roll of silver foil catching the light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一卷反射光线的银色铝箔。

branches.cn: 电解提炼的元素

branches.cn: 它在元素周期表中的位置

branches.cn: 包食物的铝箔

branches.cn: 回收的饮料罐

intro.en: A scientific name with a Latin base and a family of related technical words.
intro.cn: 这是带拉丁词基的科学名称，周围有一族技术词汇。

latinIntro.en: The base alumen is Latin, and the suffix follows the pattern of element names.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 alumen 属拉丁语，后缀沿用元素命名的模式。
